## Inspiration
- GitHub Trending: thedotmack/claude-mem — "Persistent Context Across Sessions for Every Agent — Captures everything your agent does during sessions, compresses it with AI, and injects relevant context back into future sessions" (~119k stars). earendil-works/pi — "AI agent toolkit: unified LLM API, agent loop, TUI, coding agent CLI" (123k stars). Context management and bounded agent loops are a live frontier.
- arXiv / Papers with Code: offline during this run (no fresh signal).
- npm Trending: stale 2022 data — not a viable fresh signal.
- mw-xv primitive: `packages/ai-runtime/src/memory-evaluator.ts` (MemoryCandidateRecord with confidenceBps, dataClassification, expiresAt), `packages/ai-runtime/src/sleep-dream.ts` (NonRemConsolidation with importanceBps/retrievalConfidenceBps decay), `packages/ai-runtime/src/classification-router.ts` (cloud_eligible/local_only/restricted).
URL: https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem

## The Gap
mw-xv has a sophisticated memory system (episodic/semantic/procedural candidates, salience scoring, decay, consolidation) and a classification router, but it has **no token-budget or context-tariff enforcement** for agent runs. There is no concept of a per-run token ceiling, per-topic token allocation, context budget exhaustion policy, or tariff that charges different memory classes (episodic vs semantic vs procedural) different context "prices." Every agent run accumulates context without a built-in budget mechanism — the inverse of what bounded, predictable agent loops require.

## Sketch
Add a `ContextTariff` / token-budget primitive to `@moonwitness/ai-runtime` that enforces a per-agent-run context ceiling. Design:
- `TokenBudget` with per-run `maxTokens`, per-class weights (episodic/semantic/procedural with different tariff rates), and a remaining-budget tracker.
- `enforceContextBudget(memoryItems, budget): ContextTariffResult` — selects items under the tariff (greedy by salience per token), returns admitted items, evicted items, total charged tokens, and a `budgetExhausted` flag plus an eviction rationale.
- Reuse `MemoryCandidateRecord.confidenceBps` and `classification-router` data classification so restricted/local_only memories carry higher tariff (cheaper to keep local, more expensive to cloud-egress).
- Emit a new `contextBudgetExhausted` event that downstream consumers (agent-runner, memory-evaluator) react to — e.g. trigger sleep-dream consolidation or refuse the run.
- Keep it pure/read-only (no mutation), deterministic, and testable with synthetic memories spanning the importance/confidence spectrum.

## Why Antislop
Mainstream hype chases larger context windows, bigger parameter counts, "remember everything." The contrarian position: the real bottleneck is not acquisition but *allocation*. Strategic, enforced forgetting under a token budget is higher-leverage than any amount of context-window budget. This is weird because the industry acts as if context is infinite; it's high-leverage because a simple tariff algorithm yields immediate, measurable reductions in context-drift errors and cost.

## First Spike Task
- File: `packages/ai-runtime/src/context-tariff.ts` (new). Function: `enforceContextBudget(memories: MemoryCandidateRecord[], budget: TokenBudget): ContextTariffResult`.
- Test: `packages/ai-runtime/tests/context-tariff.test.ts` — verify top-K admission by salience-per-token, eviction rationale, and deterministic budget-exhausted flag with synthetic memories.
- Run: `pnpm test:unit --filter ai-runtime`

## References
- https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem (persistent compressed context across sessions, ~119k stars)
- https://github.com/earendil-works/pi (AI agent toolkit, agent loop, 123k stars)
- packages/ai-runtime/src/memory-evaluator.ts — MemoryCandidateRecord, confidenceBps
- packages/ai-runtime/src/sleep-dream.ts — importanceBps, retrievalConfidenceBps, decay
- packages/ai-runtime/src/classification-router.ts — data classification
- GitHub search: no open issues matching "token budget", "token tariff", "context budget", "context tariff" in mw-xv
title: [IDEA] Context Tariff: Token-Budget Enforcement for Bounded Agent Runs

## Inspiration
- GitHub Trending: morluto/rea — "Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries" (477,811 stars, TypeScript, pushed 2026-11-25). Agentic repos are pushing into reverse engineering / binary analysis.
- arXiv / Papers with Code: offline during this run (no fresh signal).
- npm Trending: stale 2022 data — not a viable fresh signal.
- mw-xv primitive: `packages/ai-runtime/src/repo-inspector.ts` (`ReadOnlyRepoInspector`) and `packages/ai-runtime/src/repo-snapshot.ts` (`buildRepoSnapshot`) already build read-only, allowlisted, hash-verified snapshots of *source* repos (manifests, scripts, docs, entry points), with stack-tag inference (node/typescript/rust/go/python).
URL: https://github.com/morluto/rea

## The Gap
mw-xv inspects repositories at the *source* level only. `repo-inspector`/`repo-snapshot` list files, read text, parse manifests, and emit stack tags — but they cannot touch native binaries (ELF, Mach-O, PE), disassemble, extract imported symbols, measure section entropy, or record binary provenance. The AI runtime's agent stack (classification router, sleep-dream consolidation, memory-evaluator approvals) has no concept of binary provenance or a reverse-engineering path. Agentic reverse engineering is a fast-moving frontier (morluto/rea, openclaw/openclaw 395k stars) and mw-xv has nothing in this area.

## Sketch
Add a `BinaryInspector` primitive to `@moonwitness/ai-runtime` that, given an allowlisted path to a native binary, emits a read-only binary observation record: file type/magic, architecture, section list with sha256 per section, imported symbols, entropy per section, and a binary provenance hash (content sha256 + timestamp). Reuse the existing `RedactionContext` and `ProviderError` policy pattern (path-traversal guards, allowlist roots, max bytes) from `repo-inspector.ts` so the inspector stays read-only, sandboxed, and never executes or writes the target binary. Wire it into `buildRepoSnapshot` as an optional binary-observation pass when a binary entry point is detected, emitting a new `RepoObservationKind` of `'binary'`. Tie binary records into the AI runtime approval flow (`isValidProviderEndpoint` / `assertSafeCapabilityIdentifier`) so an agent can only analyze binaries within its company scope and classification.

## Why Antislop
Mainstream AI hype treats agents as code-writing chatbots that read source; the contrarian position is that the richest signal in a repo is often the *compiled artifact* — what actually ships. Reverse engineering is treated as a niche security specialty rather than a first-class agent primitive. This is weird because binaries are deterministic, hashable, and safer to analyze than untrusted source (read-only, no execution). It's high-leverage: a bounded binary inspector gives mw-xv agents a verifiable "what actually shipped" view without new dependencies.

## First Spike Task
- File: `packages/ai-runtime/src/binary-inspector.ts` (new). Function: `inspectBinary(path: string, ctx: BinaryInspectorContext): Promise<BinaryObservation>` — read-only magic/architecture/sections/imports/entropy/provenance hash.
- Test: `packages/ai-runtime/tests/binary-inspector.test.ts` — verify read-only behavior, allowlist enforcement, and deterministic sha256 on a small fixture binary.
- Run: `pnpm test:unit --filter ai-runtime`

## References
- https://github.com/morluto/rea (agentic reverse engineering, 477k stars)
- packages/ai-runtime/src/repo-inspector.ts — existing read-only allowlisted repo inspection pattern
- packages/ai-runtime/src/repo-snapshot.ts — buildRepoSnapshot + stack-tag inference
- packages/ai-runtime/src/classification-router.ts — data classification / cloud egress policy
- GitHub search: no open issues matching "binary", "disassemble", "decompile", "elf", "mach-o", "binary provenance", "reverse engineer" in mw-xv
title: [IDEA] Binary Inspector: Read-Only Native Binary Provenance for Agentic Reverse Engineering

body:
## Context
Created comprehensive routines reference for social media operations at `docs/operations/social-media-routines.md`. Documents 20 recurring routines across daily, weekly, bi-weekly, monthly, quarterly, and event-driven cadences.

## Scope
- [ ] Review routines document for completeness
- [ ] Assign owners for each routine
- [ ] Set up automation infrastructure (GitHub Actions, workers, webhooks)
- [ ] Configure platform API credentials in GitHub Secrets
- [ ] Create missing scripts listed in tooling requirements

## Document Contents
**Daily (3):** Metrics sync, scheduled post dispatcher, YouTube comment monitor
**Weekly (4):** Content calendar review, episode production kickoff, derivative sprint, community engagement hour
**Bi-weekly (2):** Asset pipeline health check, platform API health check
**Monthly (3):** Metrics review, newsletter digest, content calendar planning
**Quarterly (3):** Strategy review, brand asset audit, community health assessment
**Event-driven (5):** Release posts, feature launches, conference speaking, incident comms, viral amplification

## Automation Architecture
| Routine | Trigger | Tool/Script | Output Location |
|---------|---------|-------------|-----------------|
| Metrics Sync | Cron (daily 07:00) | `sync-metrics.mjs` | Content calendar |
| Post Dispatcher | Queue poll (2hr) | `post_social` worker | Platform APIs |
| Comment Monitor | Cron (30min) | `youtube-comments.mjs` | Discord #community-support |
| Asset Validation | Cron (bi-weekly) | `validate-social-assets.mjs` | CI gate / GitHub issue |
| API Health | Cron (bi-weekly) | `check-social-apis.mjs` | Discord #social-alerts |
| Release Posts | GitHub Release webhook | `render-social.mjs` + worker | All platforms |
| Episode Derivatives | YouTube upload webhook | `generate-episode-derivatives.mjs` | All platforms |

## Implementation Priority
- **Phase 0** (Week 1-2): Release posts automation (depends on SM-002)
- **Phase 1** (Week 2-3): Core daily/weekly routines (depends on SM-032, SM-023)
- **Phase 2** (Week 3-4): Monitoring & health checks
- **Phase 3** (Week 4-12): Monthly/quarterly reviews
- **Phase 4** (Week 12+): Mature operations, event-driven routines

## References
- Grand Plan: `docs/operations/social-media-grand-plan.md`
- Routines Doc: `docs/operations/social-media-routines.md`
- TaskOS: SM-032 (calendar), SM-035 (analytics), SM-023 (derivatives), SM-030/031 (scheduler)

body:
## Anti-slop check
Mainstream version: "AI generates Prisma/Drizzle schema from prompt" — one-shot LLM codegen, no verification, drifts from reality.  
This idea: **Requirements → Formal Spec → Verified Addon Manifest** using closed-loop synthesis (SpecSyn-style) where each generated model/field/relation/access is checked against the *running database* and *existing addon dependency graph* before commit — the addon either installs cleanly or the synthesis fails with a precise counterexample.

## What trending projects do
- **MetaObjects** — Generates typed models/API/UI/prompts from a single model, but **fails the build** on drift; no iterative synthesis loop, no database-grounded verification. [1](https://gh.poscat.moe/metaobjectsdev/metaobjects)
- **Evolutility**, **Steedos**, **Frappe** — Metadata-driven CRUD from JSON/YAML models; human authors the metadata, no LLM synthesis.
- **Drizzle/Prisma/TypeORM codegen** — Introspects *existing* DB to generate TS types; reverse direction (requirements → schema) is not verified.
- **GitHub trending "AI agent skills"** — Skills like `cloudflare/security-audit-skill` run multi-phase checks, but on *code*, not on *declarative schema with live DB constraints*.

## Research anchor
- **SpecSyn: LLM-based Synthesis and Refinement of Formal Specifications for Real-world Program Verification** (arXiv:2604.21570) — LLMs generate/refine formal specs; uses **semantic-non-equivalent program mutations** and **variant discrimination** to verify >90% precision / >75% recall on 1,421 real-world properties. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.21570)
- **Automating Database-Native Function Code Synthesis with LLMs** (arXiv:2604.06231) — Three-component pipeline: pseudo-code plan → hybrid fill-in-the-blank → **three-level progressive validation** (syntax, standards compliance, LLM-guided *semantic* verification). [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.06231)
- **LYNX: Analytical Program Synthesis via Grounding and Closed-Loop Refinement** (arXiv:2610.14777) — Multi-agent: planner → generator → verifier → refiner; **schema grounding** enforced by specialized agent. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14777)
- **How well do LLMs comprehend and design relational database schemata?** (arXiv:2611.17044) — Benchmark shows **explicit completeness requests** dramatically improve referential integrity F1 (0.228 → 0.909). [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17044)

## Proposed feature for MoonWitness
**Where:** New package `@moonwitness/orm-ai-synthesis` (or under `packages/ai-runtime`), consuming `@moonwitness/orm`, `@moonwitness/orm-base`, `@moonwitness/types`

**Behavior:**
1. **Input:** Natural-language requirements (e.g., "Add a purchase order model with lines, linked to vendor partner, with approval workflow and multi-company isolation").
2. **Phase 1 — Spec Synthesis (SpecSyn-style):** LLM produces a **formal addon manifest sketch** (JSON) with models, fields, relations, access, views, menus — *not* TypeScript code. Uses the existing `defineModel`/`defineAddon` *shape* as the formal language.
3. **Phase 2 — Grounding & Verification (LYNX-style):**
   - **Schema Grounding Agent:** Checks every `belongsTo`/`hasMany` against *currently installed models* in the target company's database (via `orm` introspection). Rejects references to non-existent models.
   - **Constraint Verification Agent:** Runs the sketch through the **addon installer in dry-run mode** (new `validateAddon` API) inside a savepoint transaction — validates: type compatibility, unique constraints on non-empty tables, required-field defaults, access-grant consistency, cyclic dependency detection.
   - **Completeness Agent (from 2611.17044):** Explicitly asks for missing pieces (e.g., "You referenced `vendor.partner` but no `access_group` grant for `user` role — add?").
4. **Phase 3 — Closed-Loop Refinement:** If any verification fails, the error (with precise JSON pointer via `pointerForIssue`) feeds back to the Spec Synthesis LLM for a targeted patch — repeats until valid or max iterations.
5. **Phase 4 — Commit:** Valid manifest is passed to `installAddons` for real — same transactional path as human addon upgrades, with audit/outbox.

**Why it fits MoonWitness:**
- MoonWitness already has: `defineModel`/`defineAddon` as a **formal declarative language**, `installAddons` with dependency sorting & validation, `pointerForIssue` for precise errors, multi-company isolation, additive-only schema policy.
- The synthesis target is **not raw SQL or TypeScript** — it's the *same manifest format humans write*, so the output is readable, reviewable, and version-controllable.
- Reuses the **entire existing verification pipeline** (dry-run installer) instead of building a new one.

## Why anti-mainstream / anti-pasaran
- Mainstream: "LLM writes Prisma schema" → **unverified, drifts, no transactional install**.
- This: **LLM writes manifest → verified against live DB & addon graph → installed transactionally**.
- The "formal language" is the **existing addon manifest** — no new DSL, no codegen step.
- Verification is **not a separate linter** — it's the *actual installer* in dry-run mode.

## Risk / why most teams won't build it
Requires running LLM synthesis *against a live database* (even in dry-run) — most teams isolate LLMs from DB. MoonWitness's transactional savepoint dry-run makes it safe, but the architecture is unusual. Also needs careful prompt engineering for the "formal manifest" output format.

## Links
- SpecSyn paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.21570
- DB-native function synthesis: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.06231
- LYNX closed-loop synthesis: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14777
- Schema comprehension benchmark: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17044
- MetaObjects: https://gh.poscat.moe/metaobjectsdev/metaobjects
title: [IDEA] Deterministic Schema Synthesis from Requirements: SpecSyn-Grounded Addon Generator

body:
## Anti-slop check
Mainstream version: Agent memory = vector store + chat history + RAG over past conversations.  
This idea: Agent memory = **declarative schema evolution** — every agent interaction that proposes a model change (new field, relation, constraint, access rule) is captured as an addon upgrade transaction with full audit, outbox, and rollback, making the *domain model itself* the versioned, inspectable, reversible memory of what the agent learned/did.

## What trending projects do
- **vastsa/PI-Desktop**, **nightly-labs/openbot**, **cc-haha** — Local-first AI agent desktops storing memory as local vector DBs (SQLite + embeddings) or flat JSON files; no schema versioning, no transactional guarantees. [1](https://github.com/sifted-network/sifted-awesome-ai-agents)
- **AnyProto/Any**, **sqlite-sync** — CRDT-based local-first sync for "agent memory" but memory is opaque blobs; schema changes require manual migration. [2](https://github.com/anyproto/any)
- **Git4Data (arXiv:2609.02106)** — Database-native version control for agents, but targets generic SQL, not a metadata-driven ORM with declarative addon upgrades.

## Research anchor
- **Git4Data: Database-Native Version Control for AI Agents** (arXiv:2609.02106) — Extends SQL with `SNAPSHOT`, `TAG`, `BRANCH`, `MERGE` as first-class operations so LLM agents can version data *and schema* natively within transactions. [PDF](https://borowiecki.dev/pdf/2609.02106)
- **APG: Agentic Static-Analysis Infrastructure on LLVM-IR Graph Databases** (arXiv:2611.02349) — Agents query structural code info via graph DB; shows agents can operate on *structured representations* not just text. [PDF](https://arxiv.cnoctave.top/pdf/2611.02349)
- **A Datalog Framework for CRDTs** (arXiv:2605.31569) — Declarative CRDT semantics; suggests schema-level operations can be reasoned about declaratively. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.31569)

## Proposed feature for MoonWitness
**Where:** `packages/orm`, `packages/orm-base`, `apps/api` (addon installer), `packages/ai-runtime` (new or existing)

**Behavior:**
1. Extend the addon manifest with an optional `agentMemory` section that declares which model changes an agent is allowed to propose (e.g., `allow: ['field.add', 'relation.add', 'access.grant']`).
2. When an agent (via `@moonwitness/ai-runtime` or MCP) proposes a schema change, the API routes it through the **existing addon installer** (`installAddons`) as a *versioned upgrade transaction* — same code path as human-driven addon upgrades.
3. The upgrade transaction:
   - Creates a `base.schema_version` record (new model) capturing: agent ID, prompt hash, proposed diff (JSON pointer via existing `pointerForIssue`), resulting manifest version, audit log entry, outbox event.
   - Runs validation (typecheck, constraint check, access check) inside the transaction — if it fails, full rollback.
   - On success, emits `base.outbox_event` for downstream consumers (audit UI, notification, other agents).
4. Board gets a **"Schema History"** tab (under `/board/settings` or `/board/m/base.schema_version`) showing the agent-driven evolution timeline with diff, actor (agent vs human), and one-click revert (via new downgrade transaction).

**Why it fits MoonWitness:**
- MoonWitness already has: declarative models (`defineModel`), transactional addon install/upgrade, audit/outbox in same transaction, JSON-pointer helpers, multi-company isolation, RBAC.
- This doesn't need a new migration system — it *reuses* the addon upgrade mechanism.
- The "agent memory" becomes queryable, auditable, and reversible like any other business data.

## Why anti-mainstream / anti-pasaran
- Every other project treats agent memory as **unstructured embeddings/chat logs**. This makes the **domain model itself** the memory — structured, typed, transactional, auditable.
- No separate "vector store for agent memory" — the PostgreSQL database *is* the agent memory, with the same guarantees as invoice data.
- Reverts are not "delete the embedding" — they're **transactional downgrades** with the same upgrade hooks.

## Risk / why most teams won't build it
Requires trusting agents with DDL-equivalent power; most teams sandbox agents to read-only or pre-approved tool calls. MoonWitness's additive-only schema policy (no destructive changes) and transactional installer mitigate this, but the mental model shift is large.

## Links
- GitHub trending AI agent desktops: [sifted-awesome-ai-agents](https://github.com/sifted-network/sifted-awesome-ai-agents)
- Git4Data paper: https://borowiecki.dev/pdf/2609.02106
- APG paper: https://arxiv.cnoctave.top/pdf/2611.02349
- CRDT Datalog paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.31569
title: [IDEA] Schema-Versioned Agent Memory: Domain Model as Evolving Agent State

body:
## Status

Maintainer-requested implementation proposal for the Antigravity **Desktop App**. This is an integration adapter, not a request to move Antigravity sessions into an SDK.

Before implementation, register this work as a new source-backed TaskOS task and synchronize its generated issue metadata. **Do not append tasks to or rewrite the frozen root `todo-desktop.md` checklist**: the repository explicitly retains it as historical evidence for the completed 128 `DSK-` records.

## Goal

Capture Antigravity Desktop lifecycle/tool events and display them as a live activity flow in MoonWitness, using the existing Desktop event stream and AI telemetry foundations. The integration must be opt-in, local-first, read-only, privacy-preserving, and must never change Antigravity's execution decisions.

## Repository findings (checked against `dev`)

- `apps/desktop` is already the Tauri v2 + Node 24 local-first execution host; do not create another desktop shell or agent runner.
- `apps/desktop/src/bridge.ts` already exports `DesktopEventStreamHub`, with subscriptions, bounded buffers/backpressure, filtering and disposal.
- `packages/ai-runtime/src/risk-policy.ts` already defines `GenAiTelemetryEvent`, `GenAiTelemetryCollector`, and redaction-backed event handling.
- `apps/desktop/src/local-api-server.ts` is the existing loopback Fastify host and is the natural ingress boundary for an external hook process.
- `apps/board/src/app/board/ai/hq/page.tsx` already has a Telemetry Stream area that can be assessed/reused for the live view.
- Existing `AUD-012` covers the broader PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY + Fastify SSE eventing layer. Reuse that contract when available; do not implement a competing event bus or duplicate its central API scope.
- No Antigravity-specific hook receiver/configuration was found in the inspected Desktop source tree.

**Inspected dev SHA:** `1bd4ca4adbc49128f985963f0fa959412c83c3ee`.

## Antigravity Desktop integration surface

Google documents hooks for the Antigravity App (not SDK-only):

- Global config: `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json` (Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\\.gemini\\config\\hooks.json`).
- Workspace config: `.agents/hooks.json`.
- Events: `SessionStart`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PreInvocation`, `PostInvocation`, and `Stop`.
- Hook command receives event JSON on stdin and returns a JSON response on stdout.
- `PostToolUse` includes tool-call details, step index and optional error; common context includes conversation ID, workspace paths and model name.

Official documentation: https://antigravity.google/docs/hooks

## Proposed implementation

1. **TaskOS registration first**
   - Add a new source-owned Desktop integration task without modifying frozen `todo-desktop.md`.
   - Update the deterministic TaskOS source projection, schema/tests and canonical registry through the normal reviewed workflow.
   - Keep this issue as the discussion/triage record; do not invent a TaskOS task ID before that registration exists.

2. **Install/configure an observer hook**
   - Provide an explicit opt-in install/uninstall or config-generation path for Antigravity Desktop.
   - Safely merge only the MoonWitness hook group into existing `hooks.json`; preserve unrelated user/plugin hook groups and refuse destructive overwrite.
   - Support the Windows global path and optionally workspace-level installation.
   - Use a bounded timeout and a command path that works from Antigravity's hook working directory.

3. **Implement a small hook receiver**
   - Add a dedicated Desktop CLI hook subcommand/handler that reads one JSON event from stdin, validates it against known event shapes, normalizes it, and forwards it to the running local Desktop host.
   - Use an authenticated loopback-only ingress on the existing `LocalApiServer` (or an equivalent existing Desktop IPC boundary). Do not expose a public listener or accept arbitrary destination URLs.
   - If MoonWitness Desktop is not running, exit safely and quickly; Antigravity must continue normally.

4. **Normalize and stream events**
   - Map session start/stop, model invocation start/end, tool start/completion/failure into stable MoonWitness event kinds.
   - Correlate by Antigravity conversation ID, invocation number and step index; deduplicate retries and tolerate out-of-order delivery.
   - Feed the existing `DesktopEventStreamHub` and current GenAI telemetry contract; do not create a second event bus or a parallel run database.
   - Reuse/extend the existing Telemetry Stream UI to show active sessions, current tool, recent timeline, success/failure and last-seen status.

5. **Document operating behavior**
   - Explain install, enable/disable, uninstall, Windows config path, supported event coverage, troubleshooting and privacy behavior.
   - Clearly state that hooks provide lifecycle/tool telemetry, not token-by-token model streaming or hidden chain-of-thought.

## Privacy and safety requirements

- Never persist or forward `lastUserInput`, prompt text, transcript contents, raw tool arguments, shell command text, tool output, artifact contents, credentials or environment values.
- Allowlist only required metadata (event name, conversation correlation ID, model identifier, tool name, step/invocation indexes, timestamp, coarse outcome/error class). Any displayed file path must be workspace-relative and redacted; omit it by default until a safe allowlist is proven.
- Run all event fields through the existing redaction utilities before logging, storing or displaying them.
- Do not write transcript files or read Antigravity's private brain directory as a substitute for the hook API.
- Observer hooks must not inject prompts/steps, rewrite tool arguments, deny/approve tools, force continuation, or alter Stop behavior. Return the documented neutral/pass-through response for each hook event.
- Use short bounded local delivery, bounded queues/backpressure and idempotency. No external network egress from the collector.
- Configuration changes must be reversible and preserve all unrelated user settings.
- Add adversarial tests for malformed/oversized stdin, secret-bearing fields, path traversal, spoofed requests, missing local host, queue overflow and duplicate events.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A documented opt-in installer/config generator adds the MoonWitness observer group to Antigravity App hooks without deleting or rewriting unrelated configuration.
- [ ] Windows global configuration path is covered by tests/documentation; workspace-level mode is optional and scoped to the selected repository.
- [ ] All six documented lifecycle events are parsed and normalized; tool events preserve tool name, step index and coarse outcome without retaining raw arguments.
- [ ] Authenticated loopback ingress rejects non-loopback, unauthenticated, malformed and oversized requests.
- [ ] Normalized events reach the existing Desktop event stream and are visible in the live Telemetry Stream UI without manual refresh.
- [ ] Hook failures/timeouts or a stopped MoonWitness host never block or change Antigravity's normal agent execution.
- [ ] No prompt, reasoning, transcript, raw tool args/output, secret or absolute user path is persisted or emitted.
- [ ] Redaction, bounded buffering, backpressure, deduplication, disposal and error handling have focused tests.
- [ ] Existing Desktop harness, AI runtime, Board and security tests remain green.
- [ ] Documentation explicitly describes limitations: event/lifecycle observability only; no hidden reasoning capture or guaranteed token-level stream.
- [ ] TaskOS source projection, validation and issue-sync invariants pass after the new task is registered.

## Suggested validation

- `pnpm --filter @moonwitness/desktop typecheck`
- `pnpm --filter @moonwitness/desktop test`
- `pnpm --filter @moonwitness/ai-runtime test`
- focused Board UI tests for the Telemetry Stream view
- `pnpm test:taskos`
- `pnpm tasks:validate`
- `pnpm tasks:sweep -- --check`
- `pnpm format:check`
- `pnpm verify`

## Guardrails for the implementing agent

- Work on `dev` only; no feature branches.
- Inspect the exact checkout SHA, current git status and existing hooks before editing.
- Keep changes within the Desktop integration and explicitly registered TaskOS source scope; ask the coordinator for a separate task if shared files exceed that scope.
- Do not add the Antigravity SDK as a dependency merely to read Desktop hooks.
- Do not claim the issue complete until the live Desktop-to-Board event path is demonstrated on Windows and the exact commit/CI evidence is recorded.
- Commit subject must include the registered TaskOS ID once one exists; reference this issue in the PR with `Refs #<issue-number>` (do not auto-close by default).
title: [PROPOSAL] Bridge Antigravity Desktop hooks into MoonWitness Live Agent Flow

## Background

A fresh, complete paginated ChatGPT Library listing was performed on 2026-11-23 using the connected Library listing capability. Pagination was exhausted after nine pages. The current snapshot contains:

| Scope | Entries |
|---|---:|
| Unique paths across the recursive listing | 1,670 |
| Files | 1,667 |
| Folders | 3 |
| Root-level files | 1,442 |
| Nested files | 225 |

The listing reported no repeated paths. File-type counts were 1,241 PNG, 165 Markdown, 135 ZIP, 55 JSON, 8 DOCX, 6 XLSX, 17 TXT, 6 MP4, 3 PDF, 3 JPG, 3 TS, 3 JS, 8 HTML, 2 WAV, 1 TSX, 1 SQLite, 6 SHA-256 and 1 SQL.

This differs materially from the previous archive register snapshot (319 recursive entries / 300 files / 19 folders / 203 PNG). The current top-level folder set also does not include the `/MoonWitness` path referenced by [#182](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/182). A failed path lookup is **not** proof that the folder or its contents were deleted; the discrepancy must remain unresolved until a source owner or another authoritative snapshot explains it.

## Original intent

Preserve every relevant idea and artifact with traceable source references while avoiding false claims that a Library listing is a complete ChatGPT account export, that file captions are original prompts, or that assets are cleared for publication.

## Evidence and source references

- Current complete recursive Library listing on 2026-11-23; nine pages, cursor exhausted; 1,670 unique paths.
- Existing [Library Source Register](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/blob/dev/docs/knowledge/idea-archive/LIBRARY-SOURCE-REGISTER.md), whose 319-entry inventory is now a historical snapshot pending reconciliation.
- [Total Idea Archive parent issue #183](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/183).
- [22-file MoonWitness Library pack review #182](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/182) — related path-discrepancy investigation, not replaced by this issue.
- [Private provenance index for the previously observed 203 PNGs #185](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/185) — its per-image scope remains distinct.
- [Private ChatGPT export intake #187](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/187) — a full account export remains a separate source-intake dependency.

## Objective

Reconcile the current Library metadata census with the existing source register and keep the archive's source-coverage claims accurate, privacy-aware and reproducible.

## Scope

1. Produce a dated, private/local metadata manifest for the 1,670 unique Library paths, retaining file type, size and available non-sensitive metadata.
2. Reconcile the new census against the previous 319-entry snapshot without interpreting count differences as deletion/addition of particular assets.
3. Identify why the former `/MoonWitness` folder reference is not present in the current returned path set; record the result as `UNKNOWN` unless an authoritative source resolves it.
4. Update the archive's aggregate counts and source-state notes only after the new manifest is reproducible and reviewed.
5. Keep the old 319-entry snapshot as history; do not overwrite or silently erase its provenance.
6. Separate metadata inventory from content inspection, original prompt recovery, revision history, approval, rights and publication status.
7. Publish only non-sensitive aggregate counts and a source-qualified explanation in MW-XV. Keep private paths, personal filenames, Library IDs, prompts and sensitive content in a private/local archive unless expressly cleared.

## Out of scope

- Uploading Library binaries, ZIP archives, raw private documents, private paths, Library identifiers or uncleared prompts to this public repository.
- Claiming that all 1,667 files have been opened, read, understood, deduplicated by content or rights-cleared.
- Treating generated captions or filenames as original prompts, chronology, user intent or canon.
- Deleting, renaming, modifying or moving Library objects.
- Reopening the separate legacy repository import decision or copying legacy source bytes into MW-XV.
- Replacing #182, #183, #185 or #187; each retains its own scope.

## Implementation / research notes

- Use stable local-only IDs for manifest rows; do not publish those IDs if they expose private Library references.
- Preserve a hash only where it can be computed from authorized source bytes in the private/local workflow; do not infer content hashes from metadata.
- Record path-resolution failures, unavailable files, inaccessible content and pagination errors explicitly.
- Reconcile aggregate counts with a saved snapshot and include the listing date, scope, pagination completion and counting rules.
- Keep the prior source register numbers in a historical section rather than rewriting history.
- No source-content migration or application-code change is authorized by this issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A reproducible private/local manifest contains exactly 1,670 unique paths from the dated snapshot, or documents each source item that could not be represented.
- [ ] Counts reconcile to 1,667 files and 3 folders; extension/MIME totals are internally consistent.
- [ ] The prior 319-entry / 203-PNG snapshot remains available as historical evidence.
- [ ] The `/MoonWitness` discrepancy referenced by #182 is classified as resolved with evidence or remains explicitly `UNKNOWN`; it is not described as deleted without proof.
- [ ] The public source register reflects the new aggregate census and clearly distinguishes metadata-only inventory from reviewed content.
- [ ] No private Library IDs, personal filenames, sensitive paths, prompt text or unapproved file content is committed or posted publicly.
- [ ] The work does not change application code, import source assets, alter Library objects or modify the existing #182/#183/#185/#187 ownership boundaries.
- [ ] A human reviewer accepts privacy, retention and publication boundaries before any private metadata or derived content is made public.

## Verification

- Re-run the same complete pagination and confirm the cursor is exhausted.
- Check path uniqueness and reconcile file/folder and extension totals.
- Compare the dated manifest and previous archive snapshot; report differences without assuming deletion.
- Sample-check metadata against the listing.
- Run a public-diff privacy review before updating MW-XV documentation.

## Dependencies / blocks

- **Parent:** #183 — Total Idea Archive source recovery and review.
- **Related:** #182 — prior MoonWitness folder source reference; #185 — private PNG provenance; #187 — full ChatGPT export intake.
- **Block:** owner/source review is required to resolve the missing `/MoonWitness` path and approve any publication of per-file metadata.
- **No block:** the public aggregate count and metadata reconciliation can proceed without reading all file contents.

## Exclusive ownership

Only the expanded Library metadata census and reconciliation of the archive's Library-wide aggregate counts. This issue does not own individual PNG provenance, the 22-file source pack content review, the complete ChatGPT export, story recovery, repository preservation or application implementation.

## Assigned execution agent

- **LOCAL AI:** deterministic pagination manifest, uniqueness and count checks, private/local inventory.
- **CLOUD AI:** compare prior source snapshots and identify source-register inconsistencies.
- **HUMAN REVIEW:** private-source access, retention, rights, publication and unresolved path decisions.

## Priority

**P1 — source coverage and archive integrity.**

## Background

The Total Idea Archive is currently source-bounded. The archive records one supplied 775-line master prompt and a limited set of accessible Library sources, but it does not contain a complete ChatGPT account export or every original conversation transcript.

Current evidence:

- Related repository-preservation program: [#27](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/27) (covers the legacy repository estate, not the full ChatGPT export).

The original intent is to preserve every idea, correction, revision, canon decision, creative work and historical source without replacing original wording with AI summaries.

## Parent work item


- Parent knowledge-archive completion: [#183](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/183) (this issue owns only the private ChatGPT-export intake sub-scope).

## Objective

Capture and index the complete owner-authorized ChatGPT export and any separately approved Library source material in a **private/local archive**, retaining immutable originals and traceable references for later knowledge-archive reconciliation.

## Scope

1. The owner supplies an official ChatGPT data export or another explicitly selected source package through a private/local channel.
2. Inventory conversations, timestamps, titles, message records, attachments and source metadata without assuming missing records exist.
3. Preserve original source files unchanged and produce a SHA-256 manifest plus an inventory/count report.
4. Assign stable source references to conversations and attachments; preserve original wording and chronology.
5. Classify source material for privacy, sensitivity, ownership, retention and publication eligibility.
6. Reconcile eligible, owner-approved idea references into the existing `docs/knowledge/idea-archive/` documents; retain unresolved material as unresolved rather than inventing missing context.
7. Keep the archive navigation layer linked to source references; do not create a second runtime database or duplicate project registry.

## Out of scope

- Uploading raw account exports, private conversations, personal notes, credentials or sensitive attachments to this public repository, GitHub issues, public artifacts or public CI logs.
- Treating Memory Summary, generated captions or AI reconstructions as primary source transcripts.
- Automatically changing canon, merging character identities, publishing religious interpretations or resolving owner decisions.
- Reopening the K0-006 no-legacy-import decision or importing legacy repository code/data/assets.
- Deleting, rewriting or replacing any original source.

## Intake and handling notes

- **Source classification:** private until individually reviewed and explicitly cleared.
- **Original wording:** immutable; derived summaries must link back to source references.
- **AI role:** assist with indexing and comparison only after the owner has selected the source package and privacy boundary.
- **Review authority:** HUMAN REVIEW / owner for source scope, sensitive material, canon and publication decisions.
- **TaskOS:** no managed task marker is included because this issue is a request for owner-provided source material and privacy/retention decisions, not an accepted implementation task. Any later executable work must be proposed in canonical TaskOS and synchronized through the repository workflow.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Owner-provided export/source package is received through an approved private/local channel.
- [ ] A source inventory reports captured conversation and attachment counts, available date range and any export limitations.
- [ ] Original files are retained unchanged and a SHA-256 manifest verifies their integrity.
- [ ] Every indexed source item has a stable source reference and privacy classification.
- [ ] Original messages remain distinguishable from summaries, interpretation, AI proposals and later decisions.
- [ ] Missing or conflicting source material is listed explicitly; no transcript, timestamp or canon is fabricated.
- [ ] Public repository documentation contains only metadata or derived content explicitly approved for publication.
- [ ] A human-reviewed reconciliation report links eligible source references into the existing idea archive without overwriting history.

## Verification

- Recompute SHA-256 values and compare them with the intake manifest.
- Reconcile inventory totals with the supplied export's own metadata where available.
- Spot-check source references against original files.
- Check the public diff and issue history for accidental private payloads; raw private source content must not appear there.
- Record source omissions, parser errors and unsupported attachment types as explicit limitations.

## Dependencies / blockers

- **Blocked by:** owner-provided ChatGPT export or explicitly selected source package.
- **Blocked by:** owner decision on private/local storage destination, retention and which Library items may be inspected.
- **Related:** #27 for separate legacy repository preservation; UNR-0001 through UNR-0004 for current archive/source-estate gaps.

## Ownership and priority

- **Execution lane:** HUMAN REVIEW (owner) for source provision, privacy and publication decisions; LOCAL AI may assist with deterministic indexing after approval.
- **Priority:** P0 — source preservation.
- **Exclusive ownership:** private source-intake package and its manifest; no ownership of application code or existing public archive documents until a reviewed change is proposed.

## Goal
Remove synchronous file I/O from the production logger path and strengthen recursive secret redaction.

## Current evidence
`packages/logger/src/index.ts` configures the file destination with `sync: true`. Its redaction list is limited to a fixed set of eight paths (authorization, cookie, password, refresh token, and access token variants), which does not cover arbitrary nested secret fields. The canonical TaskOS task scopes this work to the logger and API shutdown lifecycle.

## Exclusive scope
- `packages/logger/src/index.ts`
- `apps/api/src/server.ts`

2. Ensure graceful API shutdown flushes buffered logger output before process exit.
3. Add recursive redaction coverage for nested secrets such as token, secret, apiKey, and MW_AI_* fields, including nested headers.
4. Keep redaction fail-safe and avoid logging the unredacted value on error paths.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Logger tests prove no secret leakage through at least four nested object levels.

Create a private, metadata-only provenance index for the 203 PNG sources and link its aggregate status to the public visual archive.

## Purpose

Complete the **Total Idea Archive** from its current source-bounded snapshot to a reviewed, provenance-complete knowledge archive, while preserving the distinction between user ideas, repository facts, drafts, proposals, interpretations and unresolved material.

This is a follow-up to the first consolidation batch already committed on `dev`. It is **not** a replacement for the existing repository preservation / retirement program in [Issue #27](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/27), and it must not duplicate its repository-mirroring or legacy-retirement work.

## Current baseline

The first archive is available under:

- [Master archive index](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/blob/dev/docs/knowledge/idea-archive/README.md)
- [Idea catalog](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/blob/dev/docs/knowledge/idea-archive/IDEA-CATALOG.md)
- [Project registry](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/blob/dev/docs/knowledge/idea-archive/PROJECT-REGISTRY.md)
- [Canon registry](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/blob/dev/docs/knowledge/idea-archive/CANON-REGISTRY.md)
- [Story / character Bible](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/blob/dev/docs/knowledge/idea-archive/STORY-CANON-CHARACTER-BIBLE.md)
- [Religion / philosophy archive](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/blob/dev/docs/knowledge/idea-archive/RELIGION-PHILOSOPHY-ARCHIVE.md)
- [Creative / visual Bible](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/blob/dev/docs/knowledge/idea-archive/CREATIVE-VISUAL-BIBLE.md)

- [Execution roadmap](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/blob/dev/docs/knowledge/idea-archive/EXECUTION-ROADMAP.md)

- [Audit status report](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/blob/dev/docs/knowledge/idea-archive/AUDIT-STATUS-REPORT.md)
- [Issue index](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/blob/dev/docs/knowledge/idea-archive/ISSUE-INDEX.md)

The current snapshot is explicitly **PARTIAL / SOURCE-BOUNDED**. The canonical index is [the live archive README](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/blob/dev/docs/knowledge/idea-archive/README.md), and the verified follow-up inventory is in the [Issue Index](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/blob/dev/docs/knowledge/idea-archive/ISSUE-INDEX.md) and [Library Source Register](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/blob/dev/docs/knowledge/idea-archive/LIBRARY-SOURCE-REGISTER.md). It records 72 stable idea records, 26 project entries, 16 explicit canon rules, 19 character records, a 280-repository metadata census (148 public and 132 private), a selected 30-repository README/root-tree review, 161 indexed issues (66 open / 95 closed), 26 PRs, and a 637-record TaskOS `dev` registry (468 done / 49 doing / 96 todo / 24 blocked). The Library pagination now records 279 root entries and 319 recursive entries, including 203 root PNGs; contents and rights are not implied by metadata. These figures describe the audited snapshot, not proof that all historical sources or implementation states have been recovered.

## Scope

### 1. Recover missing primary sources

- Accept a user-provided ChatGPT/account export, local archive or additional source files through a scoped, explicit intake.
- Inventory each newly available source with stable source ID, source kind, date/version, owner, access status, privacy class, rights/retention constraints and checksum where applicable.
- Recover original prompt wording, dated revisions, source images, story manuscripts and character sheets only where the owner supplies or authorizes access.
- Keep private/personal material private by default. Never copy diaries, private conversations, witness records, credentials or sensitive details into this public repository without a separate explicit review and authorization.
- Treat Library captions and memory summaries as discovery hints, not substitutes for original prompts or transcripts.

### 2. Reconcile ideas, projects and histories

- Update the idea catalog, project registry and chronology from newly verified sources without creating duplicate identities for repeated mentions.
- Preserve original labels, spelling, casing and wording; place editorial rewrites in separate fields.
- Record the source and confidence for every relationship between projects, repositories, brands, characters, aliases and frameworks.
- Keep MoonWitness generations (II, XII, XIV/V10, XV) version-distinct unless source evidence and owner review approve a relationship.
- Keep separate projects separate until their relationship is demonstrated; do not infer identity from similar names.

### 3. Review canon, story and religious / philosophical material

- Resolve story, character, alias, chronology and world-rule conflicts only with source evidence and owner decisions.
- Keep scripture text, edition, translation, historical context, scholarly/tradition-specific interpretation, personal reflection and creative metaphor distinct.
- Verify source editions, Arabic/other original text, translation provenance, references and rights before publishing religious-reference datasets.
- Preserve the recorded no-depiction boundaries for Allah and the prophets as binding creative constraints in the available owner context.
- Do not promote a draft, hypothesis, symbolic image, AI summary or repository README into canon or factual/theological assertion.

### 4. Close visual and asset provenance gaps

- Recover original image masters and prompt/revision chains only when supplied or authorized.
- Track source master, derived variants, hash, dimensions, creator/source, license, attribution, review status and intended consumer.
- Keep fan-art, franchise, music and trademark references as reference-only until individual rights are reviewed.
- Reuse `packages/assets`, the existing UI Catalog and current creative pipeline; do not create a second asset manager or mandatory 3D workflow.

### 5. Convert accepted outcomes into executable work

- Reconcile this proposal with Issues #15–#22 and #27 before splitting work.
- Use existing owners in Knowledge, Corpus, Research, Story, Assets, Board, Desktop and TaskOS; add no duplicate ORM, database, app, agent runtime or UI system without a demonstrated gap.
- After maintainer/owner acceptance, create small atomic records in the canonical `docs/tasks/tasks.json` on `dev`, with dependencies, acceptance criteria and source provenance.
- Generate managed task issues only through the repository's bounded workflow in `docs/roadmap/ISSUE-SYNC-CONTRACT.md`. This proposal itself is an un-managed parent decision record and must not be treated as a TaskOS task.

## Focused child issues

The following issues split source recovery into bounded units. They remain subordinate to this archive-completion proposal and preserve the parent scope without creating a second task registry:

- [#178](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/178) — recover the primary source for **Two Generations, One Toast**.
- [#179](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/179) — recover the primary source for **Chaos Before Dawn**.
- [#180](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/180) — recover the primary source for **BIRD OF A FEATHER**.
- [#181](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/181) — recover the primary source for **THUNDERSTRUCK**.
- [#182](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/182) — review the 22-file `/MoonWitness` Library source pack.
- [#185](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/185) — build a private provenance index for the 203 Library PNG sources.
- [#187](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/187) — owner-provided private ChatGPT export intake.

The child issues own distinct deliverables. #187 is the private conversation-export intake; story recovery may depend on its approved source material. #182 and #185 use separate Library source scopes.

## Out of scope / binding safeguards

- No legacy source-code, dataset, prompt-pack, fixture, asset, font, sound or private-record import under the current K0-006 decision. Any future exception requires a source-specific owner decision, rights/privacy review and a documented reopening of that gate.
- No deletion, archival, ownership transfer or retirement of a source repository as part of this issue; those gates remain in [Issue #27](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/27).
- No automatic canon, theological, legal, identity or publication approval.
- No automatic issue closure, duplicate deletion or alteration of existing human discussion.
- No release, deployment or promotion inferred from documentation being present on `dev`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A source register accounts for every additional source actually supplied or authorized, with provenance, privacy, rights and retention status.
- [ ] New records are deduplicated by stable identity while all conflicting source versions and original wording remain recoverable.
- [ ] The idea, project, history, framework, story, character, brand and visual registries are updated only where new evidence supports a change.
- [ ] Every unresolved decision has an explicit evidence gap, options, owner and state; no missing content is reconstructed as original.
- [ ] Canon, religious-reference and rights-sensitive entries have documented human review before being marked approved or publishable.
- [ ] Repository-level preservation and retirement tasks remain linked to #27 and are not duplicated here.
- [ ] Any accepted implementation scope is represented in TaskOS and synchronized through the bounded issue workflow.
- [ ] The audit report states exactly what was inspected, what remains inaccessible, what was withheld, and what was not independently verified.
- [ ] Final archive review confirms that no private or unapproved source material entered the public repository.

- #18 — Asmaul Husna reference and visual concepts
- #19 — artwork-first creative pipeline

> **Record type:** research / feasibility proposal. **Not a TaskOS-managed implementation issue.**  
> **Archive records:** `IDEA-0064`, `PRJ-0025`.

## Purpose

Preserve the preliminary **QUANTUM–FE STONE ENERGY** research and separate its practical low-temperature thermal concepts from its high-temperature ferrite / thermochemical research path. Establish an evidence and safety boundary before any physical experiment or novelty claim.

## Sources already inspected

- Library: `Quantum_FE_Stone_Research_Paper_ID.docx` and paired PDF, version 1.0 dated 17 October 2026 (14 pages; selected sections inspected).
- Library: `Quantum_FE_Stone_Research_DIY.xlsx`, 7 worksheets / 149 extracted rows.
- Research paper status: preliminary scoping review and research proposal; not peer-reviewed. It states that no physical experiment, sample synthesis or new DFT calculation was performed in that work.
- The DIY planner also states that no physical experiment was done and novelty remains unverified.

## Two research lanes — keep them separate

### A. Near-term, lower-temperature solar thermal work

The workbook proposes a recycled-aluminium-can solar air heater for useful heat (e.g. drying), not electricity. It also proposes comparing iron-rich rock, basalt / ceramic, steel and water as thermal-storage media. The paper warns against assuming iron-rich rock is automatically better; its comparison notes that water has substantially higher specific heat capacity than ordinary stone over normal temperature ranges.

Any test should compare like-for-like boundary conditions, useful heat output, heat loss, airflow / pressure drop, cost and cycle durability. Published performance numbers are not a promise for a local DIY device. Cost figures in the workbook are planning estimates, not vendor quotations.

### B. Fe-oxide / ferrite material research

The report discusses Fe–Mn–Al spinel, Fe–Mg–Al systems, cation inversion / vacancy ideas, waste iron oxide and porous ceramic supports. It also records prior art for broad Mn-substituted hercynite and Mg–Al–Fe cation-ordering families. Therefore the broad compositions must not be claimed as new material discoveries.

Ferrite redox / thermochemical hydrogen pathways involve high temperatures and specialist laboratory equipment. They are **not home DIY chemistry**. Do not synthesize ferrites, reduce oxides, handle high-temperature controlled-atmosphere reactions or attempt hydrogen production in a home experiment.

## Scope

- Pin and recheck the references and patent leads already listed in the paper.
- Separate established literature, engineering hypotheses and unverified novelty claims.
- Build a comparison matrix for low-temperature thermal-storage media.
- Review whether a safe, non-concentrating solar-air-heater proof of concept is feasible under a separate approved experimental plan.
- Reproduce the literature / prior-art search for Fe–Mn–Al and Fe–Mg–Al families before proposing any new composition claim.
- Record the need for laboratory collaboration and safety review for any high-temperature ferrite path.

## Out of scope

- No claim of a newly discovered energy source, material or “quantum energy from stone”.
- No claim that iron-rich stone outperforms water without measured, comparable data.

## Purpose

Preserve the authored CRAYON framework as a distinct, versioned concept and determine how its v1.3 baseline relates to the companion paper **“An Easy Way to Understand Allah” v2**. Do not merge either one into the separately archived **OMNISCIENCE METHOD / RGBL** framework.

- Library: `CRAYON_Framework_v1.3_Bilingual_FINAL.docx` (paired PDF), dated 23 August 2026.
- Library: `Easy_Way_to_Understand_Allah_Bilingual_Research_Paper_v2_FINAL.docx` (paired PDF).

- Separate RGBL source: `Omniscience_Method_RGBL_AI_Ready_Research_Paper.md` (17 August 2026).

## Baseline to preserve

CRAYON v1.3 defines four cumulative levels:

1. **R1 — REALITY**
2. **G2 — GOVERNING ORDER**
3. **B3 — BEING**
4. **L4 — LIGHT**

It also uses a 12 / 3 / 6 / 9 clock teaching metaphor, 9 Gate, 13 Way, situational audience conditions, quality checks and a feedback loop. The source explicitly describes CRAYON as a proposed conceptual / educational framework, not a validated scientific theory. The clock is not an evidence system, scientific measure or religious symbol. The gates are not a claim that only nine biological senses exist.

The companion v2 paper uses a different Gate 6–9 wording and a different 13-Way sequence. Preserve the source differences rather than silently rewriting one document.

**Critical distinction:** CRAYON uses **Governing Order / Being**; the RGBL paper uses **Guidance / Balance**. The shared letters do not establish that the frameworks are the same.

## Scope

- Create a source/version crosswalk between CRAYON v1.3 and the v2 companion paper.
- Preserve exact level, Gate and Way terminology from each file.
- Record the audience conditions, clock metaphor, quality checks and feedback-loop notes as authored framework content.
- Identify which companion-paper differences are application variants and which, if any, were intended as a formal revision.
- Keep empirical observations, philosophical inferences, theological identification and personal reflection distinguishable.
- Record an owner decision before changing the baseline.

## Out of scope

- No new app, ORM addon, cognitive-science taxonomy or education product.
- No claim that CRAYON proves Allah or is experimentally validated.
- No merger with OMNISCIENCE RGBL.
- No rewriting or replacing original Library files.

- [ ] Exact source/version crosswalk exists for both CRAYON documents.
- [ ] R1/G2/B3/L4 definitions and cumulative rule are retained accurately.
- [ ] v1.3 and companion-v2 Gate / 13-Way differences are explicitly compared.
- [ ] RGBL is shown as a distinct framework with different G/B meanings.
- [ ] Non-claims and evidence boundaries from the source documents are retained.
- [ ] Owner decision is recorded for any proposed baseline change.

Make A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv the sole forward development target and safely preserve, assess, selectively migrate, and retire historical bjo163 source repositories.

## Canonical documents

- Vision: https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/blob/dev/docs/strategy/MOONWITNESS-VISION.md
- Domain ownership: https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/blob/dev/docs/architecture/DOMAIN-OWNERSHIP-RECONCILIATION.md

- Target baseline: https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/blob/dev/docs/migration/TARGET-BASELINE-2026-11-22.md
- Public inventory (148 repository records): https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/blob/dev/docs/migration/inventory/bjo163-public-repositories.csv

## Work plan

### P0 — Preserve the source estate
- [ ] Confirm whether private repositories, gists, wikis, package registries, container images, releases, Pages, Actions artifacts and local-only assets exist beyond the public 148-row inventory.
- [ ] Capture exact branch/tag refs and HEAD SHAs for every in-scope repository.
- [ ] Create owner-controlled mirrors including Git LFS objects; verify restore from independent copies.
- [ ] Export issues, pull requests/comments, wiki, releases, workflows and non-Git artifacts.
- [ ] Record license, notices, third-party provenance, secrets/deployment dependencies and privacy constraints.

### P1 — Reconcile and prioritize
- [ ] Review the matrix with the platform owner and domain maintainers.
- [ ] Compare every candidate to existing ORM/addons and avoid duplicate domains/runtimes.
- [ ] Approve per-source disposition and owner.
- [ ] Prioritize corpus/RGBL, Asmaul Husna, GOD PROMISE, ROCKSOUL research, visual assets, ROCKSOUL FLOW and communication concepts.

### P2 — Migrate safely
- [ ] Create source-pinned import manifests with repo/ref/commit/path/content hash, rights evidence and target destination.
- [ ] Dry-run data imports; validate IDs, byte lengths, checksums, provenance, rights and reproducibility.
- [ ] Integrate code/assets selectively only after license/security/API checks.
- [ ] Add focused tests and exact-SHA evidence to the existing roadmap/governance process.

### P3 — Verify retirement readiness
- [ ] Prove no target runtime, CI, webhook, package consumer, website, DNS or deployment depends on an old repo marked for retirement.
- [ ] Verify archive restoration and required redirects/deprecation notices.
- [ ] Obtain explicit owner approval before archiving or closing repositories/account.

## Guardrails

- No repository deletion or account closure as part of this issue until all retirement gates pass.
- No bulk code copy and no second ORM, IAM, storage, AI runtime or UI system.
- Unknown rights mean no redistribution of source bytes.
- Personal archives, witness testimony and private conversation data require scoped consent, privacy, retention and revocation controls.
- A plan or README is not proof of implementation; record actual test/CI evidence.

## Baseline

The inventory is public repository metadata only (148 entries captured 2026-11-22). It is not a complete private-resource, code, license, privacy, security or deployment audit. The target docs are an initial decision package, not a claim that source code has already migrated.

## Purpose

Preserve the remembered **BABYDOLL — SERVICE JAM / AEQ** concept without merging it prematurely into the core MoonWitness app, addon registry, community, or XP/reward domain.

Memory notes describe AEQ as a concept intended to begin after a Hijri-year transition, using the phrases “decentralized / Allah's method” and “destroy the old, start fresh.” These are concept notes, not a verified date, technical design, religious ruling, or approved execution plan.

## Scope for this issue

- Preserve the project name and the original concept wording as source notes.
- Clarify what AEQ represents, what problem it solves, its intended users, and what “service jam” means in operational terms.
- Separate product requirements from metaphors, spiritual reflections and slogans.

# Local AI concept brief — AEQ / BABYDOLL Service Jam

## 1. Preserve the original concept without inventing missing meaning

Names and remembered wording:
- `BABYDOLL — SERVICE JAM`
- `AEQ`
- `No Plan (Just Do it)`
- `I do anything` (remembered phrase; verify intended spelling and meaning with the owner)
- `Simple Plan`
- “decentralized / Allah's method”
- “destroy the old, start fresh”

These are raw concept notes and slogans. The local agent must preserve them as source wording, then ask what each phrase means in operational language; do not silently rewrite them into a product promise, legal policy, religious statement or technical architecture.

## 2. Timing note — not a verified calendar commitment

The concept history says AEQ may begin after Hijri year 1448 ends. A previous rough note estimated:
- 1 Muharram 1448 around 26 June 2026.
- 1 Muharram 1449 around 15–16 June 2027.

These are **remembered estimates**, not authoritative dates. The local agent must select a named calendar authority / method and check the exact local date for the intended locale (Asia/Jakarta) before calculating a countdown or scheduling anything. Hijri dates can vary by method, observation and jurisdiction. Do not hard-code either estimate into production, imply that the event has been divinely scheduled, or display a countdown until a maintainer confirms the intended calendar convention.

## 3. Translate metaphors into testable product questions

- “Decentralized” — does this mean independent teams, distributed ownership, federated services, local-first data, or simply avoiding a central coordinator? These are different designs; do not assume blockchain, cryptocurrency or peer-to-peer architecture.
- “Allah's method” — preserve as the owner's spiritual framing / personal motivation. Do not represent it as a technical protocol, externally verifiable divine command, or authorization to act for others.
- “Destroy the old, start fresh” — treat as a metaphor for renewing a process, clearing obsolete plans or starting a new service cycle. It must never mean deleting production data, wiping accounts, cancelling commitments or destroying records.
- “Service Jam” — determine whether it is a service design workshop, community volunteer event, rapid prototype sprint, maintenance window or an actual service product.
- “No Plan (Just Do it)” / “Simple Plan” — resolve the apparent tension: the concept may prefer lightweight execution, but operational work still needs goals, safety checks, owners, rollback and evidence.

## 4. Discovery brief required from the owner

The local AI should prepare a short decision document with:
1. What AEQ stands for and the intended expansion of the acronym (unknown until owner confirms).
2. What BABYDOLL names: a project, event, service, campaign, product or codename.
3. Who the intended users/beneficiaries are.
4. The concrete problem or service gap.
5. What a participant actually does and what result they receive.
6. Whether it is part of MoonWitness, independent, a campaign or a temporary event.
7. What data, permissions, budget, physical logistics and safety are involved.
8. Whether any date dependency is real and which Hijri calendar convention applies.
9. What is explicitly out of scope.

Do not guess answers. Maintain an “unknown / owner decision required” section for unresolved information.

## 5. Integration boundary

Do not create an app, addon, reward ledger, payments, wallet or separate community model from this concept alone. If the owner later confirms a concrete MoonWitness use case:
- project planning and tasks remain in `orm-project`;
- review/approval state reuses `orm-workflow`;
- notices reuse `orm-notification`;
- community relationships reuse the proposed `orm-community`;
- achievements/rewards reuse the proposed `orm-experience` only when a real progression use case exists;
- content and assets remain with Knowledge / Assets.

If AEQ is independent, keep it as a separate project specification and do not add dependencies to MoonWitness core.

## 6. Safe execution boundaries

- No destructive reset, mass deletion, force push, production wipe or irreversible data operation.
- No money collection, rewards, physical meetups or exchange of personal contact details until a proper consent, safeguarding, fraud and operational policy has been reviewed.
- No unsupported claim that Allah has instructed, approved or guaranteed a technical action.
- Keep personal spiritual reflection separate from product requirements and evidence.

## 7. Acceptance

- [ ] AEQ acronym meaning is owner-confirmed or explicitly marked unknown.
- [ ] BABYDOLL / Service Jam relationship and audience are defined.
- [ ] Each slogan has an operational interpretation or remains marked “metaphor / unresolved”.
- [ ] Hijri date and timezone are verified from an identified source before scheduling.
- [ ] Integration decision (MoonWitness / independent / campaign / deferred) is approved.
- [ ] No implementation package or destructive action is proposed without a concrete, reviewed use case.

Then read the repository rules, especially `.agents/rules/learned-invariants.md`, `docs/tasks/README.md`, `docs/roadmap/ISSUE-SYNC-CONTRACT.md`, and the ADR/package documents linked above. # Concept history, plain-language explanation and real-world interpretation

## 1. What has actually been recorded

The owner's project notes contain the names:
- **BABYDOLL — SERVICE JAM**
- **AEQ**
- **No Plan (Just Do it)**
- **I do anyting** (preserve this exact remembered spelling until the owner confirms intended wording)
- **Simple Plan**
- “decentralized / Allah's method”
- “destroy the old, start fresh”

The acronym AEQ has not been expanded in the available project notes. BABYDOLL's exact relationship to AEQ is also not confirmed. This issue exists to prevent the names and intent from being lost while avoiding an invented architecture.

## 2. Possible plain-language interpretations — questions, not conclusions

The local AI may prepare options, but must label them as hypotheses:
- “Service Jam” could mean a short service-design workshop, a volunteer/community event, a rapid prototype sprint, a maintenance session, or a service product.
- “Decentralized” could refer to distributed teams, independent service ownership, local-first data, federated services or reduced central coordination. It does not automatically mean blockchain or cryptocurrency.
- “Destroy the old, start fresh” could be a metaphor for retiring outdated plans and beginning a new service cycle. It must not be interpreted as deleting production records or destroying existing commitments.
- “No Plan (Just Do it)” and “Simple Plan” may express a preference for low ceremony. Operationally, even a simple initiative needs an owner, a goal, boundaries, safety checks, a rollback and a record of what changed.

## 3. Real-world examples to distinguish the possibilities

### Example A — if Service Jam is a workshop
A small group gathers to identify a service problem, sketch a solution, prototype one workflow and gather feedback. This needs an event brief and participant safety plan, not a new ORM addon.

### Example B — if Service Jam is a service sprint
A team spends a defined period fixing one operational bottleneck. Project tasks and approvals can reuse orm-project and orm-workflow. No separate app is needed unless deployment requirements prove otherwise.

### Example C — if Service Jam is a community initiative
Participants share ideas and take part in approved community activities. If the initiative is part of MoonWitness, use the Community and Experience domains only after those are approved. Do not create a parallel social graph or XP database.

### Example D — if AEQ is independent
Keep it as a separate concept / project specification. Do not attach it to MoonWitness's login, data, rewards or deployment until there is a concrete integration reason.

These examples are decision aids. The owner must confirm which, if any, describes the intended concept.

## 4. Hijri-calendar note from the conversation history

The earlier project note connected AEQ's start to the end of Hijri 1448 and remembered rough estimates:
- 1 Muharram 1448: around 26 June 2026.
- 1 Muharram 1449: around 15–16 June 2027.

These are approximate memory notes, not a binding religious/calendar determination. The first date is already past relative to the 22 November 2026 issue baseline. Before any countdown or public schedule is created, the owner must select the calendar authority/method (for example, local official Indonesian determination versus a calculated calendar), confirm timezone Asia/Jakarta, and verify the intended event date. Do not present a computed date as divinely set or certain across all communities.

## 5. Owner decisions required

The AI agent should produce a decision sheet with explicit UNKNOWN fields:
1. What does AEQ stand for?
2. Is BABYDOLL the product, event, campaign, working title or separate initiative?
3. What does “Service Jam” mean in this context?
4. Who is the intended user / beneficiary?
5. What tangible service or outcome is delivered?
6. What does “decentralized” mean operationally?
7. What is being renewed by “destroy the old”, and what must be preserved?
8. Is a Hijri date a real dependency or just a symbolic timing note?
9. Is AEQ a MoonWitness feature, independent effort, temporary event or deferred concept?

Do not answer these on the owner's behalf.

## 6. Implementation boundary

No new application, ORM addon, payment system, wallet, reward ledger or community infrastructure should be created from AEQ notes alone. Only after a real use case is confirmed should the agent map it to Project, Workflow, Community, Experience, Knowledge or existing service owners. If none fits, bring a source-backed architecture proposal to the maintainer.

## 7. Safe operation

A “fresh start” must never trigger deletion, account reset, force-push, production wipe or loss of historical records. Use versioned plans, reversible state transitions, backups and explicit approvals. Spiritual language remains the owner's personal framing; the system must not claim divine authorization, guaranteed outcomes or authority over participants.

## Local AI execution instruction

Read the complete issue and parent architecture proposal before producing work. Read the conversation-history narrative, identify which statements are owner intent versus verified source facts, then inspect the current source tree. Do not implement based only on the text in this issue. Mark every discovered capability as EXISTS, PARTIAL, MISSING, PROPOSED or UNKNOWN and cite exact repository paths/tests. Preserve the source wording and uncertainty; never silently “complete” missing requirements by guessing.

After approval, create stable atomic TaskOS records first and follow docs/roadmap/ISSUE-SYNC-CONTRACT.md. Commit only owned paths, use the approved dev workflow, and never report success without verifiable evidence on the exact SHA.
