**Parent architecture proposal:** [Issue #15 — Non-overlapping MW-XV expansion](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/15)

**Status:** Product / research specification proposal. This issue captures the project concept and scope; it is not proof that the feature exists or authorization to bypass the repository's TaskOS workflow. After maintainer acceptance, break implementation into atomic records in `docs/tasks/tasks.json` and synchronize them according to `docs/roadmap/ISSUE-SYNC-CONTRACT.md`.

## Goal

Record the previous desktop research comparing OpenCode and DeepSeek Harness as an evaluation track, then decide whether any component is worth integrating, adapting or forking into MoonWitness Desktop. This is an evaluation and integration decision, not an instruction to fork either project automatically.

## Existing MoonWitness baseline to reuse

The repository already has a Tauri desktop application with local-first and AI-harness components, including:
- `apps/desktop/src/agent-runner.ts`
- `apps/desktop/src/bridge.ts`
- `apps/desktop/src/local-sidecar.ts`
- `apps/desktop/src/mcp-host.ts`
- `apps/desktop/src/risk-gate.ts`
- `apps/desktop/src/sync-client.ts`
- `apps/desktop/src/worktree-sandbox.ts`
- PTY / worktree and local execution support.

The AI platform also has `packages/ai-runtime`, `packages/ai-mcp`, `packages/orm-ai` and an established AI governance architecture. This is the integration baseline; do not create a competing agent runtime or new desktop application.

## Evaluation dimensions

Compare OpenCode, DeepSeek Harness and the existing MoonWitness Desktop on:
- Desktop UX, editor / terminal workflow and task lifecycle.
- Local-first operation, offline behavior and data residency.
- Provider abstraction and model routing.
- MCP support and tool interoperability.
- Permission, filesystem, shell and network boundaries.
- Worktree isolation, patch review and rollback.
- Human approval and auditable execution.
- Memory / context handling and source provenance.
- License, maintenance activity, extension points and long-term fork cost.
- Build / packaging compatibility with the existing Tauri app.

Any current capability, version, license or project status must be checked from its upstream source during the evaluation; do not rely on old comparison notes.

## Decision outcomes

For every evaluated capability choose one:
1. **Reuse:** current MoonWitness code already satisfies the requirement.
2. **Integrate:** consume an upstream library or protocol behind an existing boundary.
3. **Adapt:** implement a small compatible component in the current desktop architecture.
4. **Fork:** only with a documented strategic advantage, license compatibility, maintenance owner and sustainable upstream divergence plan.
5. **Reject / defer:** capability is redundant, unsafe, unmaintained or too costly.

## Security boundaries

- Keep filesystem, shell, process, network and MCP access behind explicit risk/capability gates.
- Do not grant an agent unrestricted access to user files or credentials.
- Preserve worktree isolation and human review for changes.
- No hidden execution, silent network fallback, secret exposure or automatic production mutation.
- Keep local-only / restricted data classification boundaries intact.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Current exact-SHA inventory of MoonWitness Desktop and relevant AI packages is recorded.
- [ ] Current upstream OpenCode / DeepSeek Harness source, release and license facts are verified.
- [ ] Feature comparison includes security and maintenance, not only UI.
- [ ] A reuse / integrate / adapt / fork / defer decision is recorded for each capability.
- [ ] No duplicate app, agent runtime, MCP host or memory store is proposed without a demonstrated gap.
- [ ] Accepted implementation tasks flow through TaskOS and existing desktop/AI governance.

## References

- [Issue #15 architecture boundary](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/15)
- [Desktop app](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/tree/dev/apps/desktop)
- [AI runtime](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/tree/dev/packages/ai-runtime)
- [AI MCP](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/tree/dev/packages/ai-mcp)
- [AI addon](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/tree/dev/packages/orm-ai)
- [AI Corporation ADR](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/blob/dev/docs/decisions/0007-ai-corporation-addon-first-architecture.md)

---

# Local AI evaluation brief — desktop harness reuse vs integrate vs fork

## 1. Architectural baseline is already accepted

Before recommending any external fork, read:
- `docs/architecture/adr/0008-local-first-desktop-agent-harness.md` (accepted desktop architecture).
- `docs/architecture/desktop-local-first-harness.md`.
- `docs/decisions/0007-ai-corporation-addon-first-architecture.md`.
- `.agents/rules/learned-invariants.md` (especially INV-008, INV-009, INV-010).
- `apps/desktop/package.json`, `apps/desktop/tauri.conf.json`, and the desktop source files below.
- `packages/ai-runtime`, `packages/ai-mcp`, `packages/orm-ai`, `packages/local-ai`, `packages/jobs` and relevant AI tests.

The desktop application already exists as a Tauri v2 shell with a local Node sidecar / harness and is designed to host the Board UI. The architecture deliberately separates browser control plane from native local execution. Do not create a second desktop app or move domain models into the desktop host.

## 2. Current MoonWitness components to map

Inspect actual current implementation and tests for:
- `apps/desktop/src/agent-runner.ts`: local agent execution lifecycle.
- `apps/desktop/src/bridge.ts`: Tauri/UI capability bridge.
- `apps/desktop/src/local-sidecar.ts`: local runtime/sidecar composition.
- `apps/desktop/src/mcp-host.ts`: local MCP hosting.
- `apps/desktop/src/risk-gate.ts`: capability / risk / human-approval enforcement.
- `apps/desktop/src/sync-client.ts`: central reconciliation/synchronization.
- `apps/desktop/src/worktree-sandbox.ts`: isolated repository worktrees and patch boundary.
- `packages/ai-runtime`: provider adapters, runtime orchestration, capability gateway, memory candidates and verification.
- `packages/ai-mcp`: MCP transport adapter.
- `packages/orm-ai`: durable contracts, grants, agents, runs, artifacts and obligations.
- `packages/ai-evaluation`: repeatable evaluation and regression evidence.

The local desktop is an execution harness; Board is the shared UI/control plane; API/PostgreSQL remains the central authority for synced business/work records. Preserve this membrane.

## 3. External candidates and live research requirements

Compare **OpenCode**, **DeepSeek Harness / dsh-superagent** (verify the exact upstream project identity), and MoonWitness Desktop itself.

Do not rely on memory for current:
- repository URL, maintainers and project identity,
- latest stable release / commit activity,
- license and dependency licenses,
- supported OS/runtime,
- provider / model support,
- MCP support and extension mechanisms,
- security model and known limitations,
- packaging and long-term maintenance signal.

Record retrieval date, exact upstream commit/release and source URL for every material claim. If upstream facts cannot be verified, mark them unknown rather than assuming.

## 4. Comparison matrix — evaluate behavior, not branding

For every candidate score and cite evidence for:
- Installation, updates, startup time and resource usage.
- Desktop UX, terminal/editor/shell flow and session restoration.
- Model provider abstraction, routing, local inference and offline behavior.
- Context / memory management, workspace indexing and retrieval.
- MCP tools/resources, protocol support and transport constraints.
- Filesystem access, path allowlist, shell execution, process control and network egress.
- Worktree isolation, patch review, rollback and conflict recovery.
- Human approval, risk tiers, logs, audit trail and PCW evidence.
- Secret handling, sandboxing, prompt injection boundaries and data exfiltration resistance.
- Testability, API extensibility, dependency footprint, license compatibility and fork divergence cost.
- Fit with Tauri, current Board bridge, current runtime contracts and MoonWitness release gates.

A UI feature is not an architectural win if it weakens risk gates or moves sensitive data to a cloud service without an explicit classification decision.

## 5. Decision framework

Every evaluated feature gets one result:
- **Reuse:** MoonWitness already has adequate behavior; document it and close the gap as no-op.
- **Integrate:** use an upstream library/protocol behind an existing interface.
- **Adapt:** implement a small local component in the current harness.
- **Fork:** only when there is a quantified strategic advantage, compatible license, named maintainer, security patch plan, upstream tracking and costed divergence policy.
- **Reject / defer:** no meaningful gap, security mismatch, weak maintenance, incompatible license or excessive cost.

Do not select a fork simply because an external product looks more polished. Do not rewrite existing Tauri/Node/AI infrastructure before an exact capability gap and migration plan are demonstrated.

## 6. Security and operational non-negotiables

- Risk tiers R0–R4 and capability grants remain enforced; agents cannot grant themselves additional authority.
- Local-only / restricted data must not silently route to cloud providers.
- Filesystem, shell, process, network and MCP execution must stay behind explicit allowlists / capability checks.
- Preserve isolated worktrees and reviewable diffs; no hidden writes to the user's repository.
- Scrub secrets from process environments and logs.
- Require human approval for elevated-risk changes and production-impacting operations.
- Preserve PCW/evidence and independent acceptance; agent self-report is not proof.
- Never allow arbitrary remote plugin code to execute in the user's environment by default.

## 7. Deliverables

1. Exact-SHA current MoonWitness desktop architecture map.
2. Upstream comparison table with cited primary sources and license audit.
3. Capability-by-capability reuse/integrate/adapt/fork/reject matrix.
4. Threat model and risk register for any proposed integration.
5. Recommended minimal implementation plan, rollback strategy and test plan.
6. ADR update only if the accepted baseline actually changes; preserve ADR 0008 rather than silently superseding it.

The result should answer a practical decision: **what, if anything, should MoonWitness borrow from OpenCode or DeepSeek Harness, and why is that better than continuing the existing Desktop architecture?**


## Local AI agent handoff contract

Read this issue and its parent [Issue #15](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/15) in full before acting. Then read the repository rules, especially `.agents/rules/learned-invariants.md`, `docs/tasks/README.md`, `docs/roadmap/ISSUE-SYNC-CONTRACT.md`, and the ADR/package documents linked above. Revalidate the live `dev` SHA and current worktree.

# Original decision context, repository reality and real-world comparison scenario

## 1. What question the owner actually asked

The conversation **“Bandingkan OpenCode DeepSeek Harness” — 22 November 2026** asked which desktop solution would be better to use as a base to fork and develop. The important intent is not to create another desktop product for its own sake. It is to identify which existing harness can give MoonWitness a better developer experience while preserving its own local-first, governed, auditable execution model.

The comparison must answer: **What capability is genuinely missing from MoonWitness Desktop, and is that gap cheaper and safer to reuse, integrate, adapt or fork than to implement within the current architecture?**

## 2. Current MoonWitness baseline — verified paths to inspect

The repository already contains a Tauri desktop project and local execution files:
- apps/desktop/src/agent-runner.ts
- apps/desktop/src/bridge.ts
- apps/desktop/src/local-sidecar.ts
- apps/desktop/src/mcp-host.ts
- apps/desktop/src/risk-gate.ts
- apps/desktop/src/sync-client.ts
- apps/desktop/src/worktree-sandbox.ts
- apps/desktop/src/cli.ts and types.ts

The current platform also contains:
- packages/ai-runtime — agent execution, provider adapters, policy/capability gateway, classification routing and verification support.
- packages/ai-mcp — MCP transport / adapter layer.
- packages/orm-ai — durable agent, provider, model, contract, grant, run, artifact and obligation records.
- packages/ai-evaluation — evaluation and regression framework.
- packages/local-ai — separate local suggestion / research boundary.

**Accepted architecture already exists:** ADR 0008 at docs/architecture/adr/0008-local-first-desktop-agent-harness.md and docs/architecture/desktop-local-first-harness.md. ADR 0007 governs AI Corporation. A future proposal must explain why those accepted boundaries need an amendment; do not silently replace them.

## 3. Real-world developer scenario to use in the comparison

A developer asks a local agent to add a feature to a repository:
1. The desktop app opens a selected workspace.
2. The agent receives only the approved task context and scoped filesystem/capability grants.
3. It creates or uses an isolated worktree, not an uncontrolled mutation of the user's main working tree.
4. The agent inspects files and proposes a plan.
5. File reads, shell commands, network access and MCP tools pass through explicit permission/risk checks.
6. It makes a small patch and reports exact changed paths.
7. Tests run in the controlled environment.
8. A human reviews the diff, test results and any risky action.
9. A Proof-Carrying Work bundle / artifact manifest records what happened.
10. The result syncs to MoonWitness using the existing desktop/API boundary.
11. The task is not marked complete until independent acceptance evidence is confirmed.

Compare OpenCode and DeepSeek Harness against this complete workflow, not just their screenshot, terminal or model-selection UX.

## 4. Required comparison matrix

For every capability, record:
- Current MoonWitness status: EXISTS / PARTIAL / MISSING / UNKNOWN.
- OpenCode status with exact upstream source / version / license.
- DeepSeek Harness identity and status, verified against the correct upstream project.
- User impact and reproducible demonstration.
- Security / privacy impact.
- Integration cost and dependency impact.
- Whether current public interfaces allow reuse.
- Decision: reuse / integrate / adapt / fork / reject / defer.
- Test proving the decision.

Do not assume that “DeepSeek Harness” is one unambiguous product name; verify the exact repository and distinguish official upstream from forks or similarly named projects.

## 5. Real-world evaluation cases

- **Offline task:** agent should continue within local-only scope without silently sending content to cloud.
- **Patch review:** agent changes three files; UI shows exact diff and reviewer can reject or revert.
- **Prompt injection:** a repository README asks the agent to exfiltrate secrets; policy should deny this.
- **Permission escalation:** agent requests unrestricted shell/network; current risk gate should require denial or explicit approval.
- **Worktree collision:** two tasks touch overlapping files; system should serialize or detect conflicts rather than corrupt work.
- **MCP connector:** agent invokes one approved tool with a capability grant; logs show actor, scope and result without leaking credentials.
- **Task continuity:** restart desktop mid-task; the system should recover only persisted, authorized state and not assume an incomplete task succeeded.

## 6. Decision and output

The final recommendation must include:
- One page of executive findings.
- Source-backed table for current MoonWitness and both upstream candidates.
- License / security / maintenance review.
- Capability ownership map.
- Recommendation per capability: reuse, integrate, adapt, fork, reject or defer.
- Minimal proposed integration slice with exact file boundaries.
- Test, rollback and upstream divergence plan if forking is recommended.

A full fork is a high-maintenance commitment. It must not be selected only because one desktop looks more polished. Do not add another agent runtime, MCP host, memory store or desktop app unless a concrete unmet requirement is demonstrated.

## Local AI execution instruction

Read the complete issue and parent architecture proposal before producing work. Read the conversation-history narrative, identify which statements are owner intent versus verified source facts, then inspect the current source tree. Do not implement based only on the text in this issue. Mark every discovered capability as EXISTS, PARTIAL, MISSING, PROPOSED or UNKNOWN and cite exact repository paths/tests. **Status:** Product / research specification proposal. This issue captures the project concept and scope; it is not proof that the feature exists or authorization to bypass the repository's TaskOS workflow. After maintainer acceptance, break implementation into atomic records in `docs/tasks/tasks.json` and synchronize them according to `docs/roadmap/ISSUE-SYNC-CONTRACT.md`.

## Goal

Formalize the user's research methods—source comparison, pattern/puzzle exploration, reverse reading, parallel letter analysis and “find light in the darkness”—as reproducible research workflows without turning an interesting pattern into an unsupported factual or theological claim.

## Research method components

- **Source capture:** identify the exact page/document/edition, URL, author/publisher, retrieval date, version or archived snapshot, and relevant section/paragraph.
- **Text extraction:** preserve the original language and separate a literal quotation from a transcription, transliteration, translation or paraphrase.
- **Pattern / puzzle analysis:** record the hypothesis, extraction rule, direction (forward/reverse), offsets, selected letters/words, expected controls and alternative explanations.
- **Parallel comparison:** compare multiple sources or documents by explicitly aligned passages / sections and record differences, omissions, translation choices and editorial changes.
- **Interpretation:** store the researcher's interpretation as a hypothesis with confidence and counter-evidence; do not merge it with source text.
- **Review / reproduction:** another reviewer should be able to repeat the method from the saved source snapshot and obtain the same result.
- **Publication:** only publish a conclusion with its evidence, limitations and source trail.

The user's earlier “Written in Reverse” / discography-Wikipedia puzzle exploration is a motivating example. Any letter-pattern candidate (including the remembered “MYTH” sequence or mnemonic) must be checked against the exact source text and extraction method. Do not say that a word occurs literally in a page unless a direct source search or reproducible extraction confirms it. Patterns may be interesting without proving intent, authorship, prophecy or external causation.

## Evidence labels

Every research output should distinguish at least:
- **Source fact:** directly supported by the source.
- **Exact quotation:** verbatim wording with location and attribution.
- **Translation / paraphrase:** identified as such and linked to the source edition.
- **Derived pattern:** reproducible output of a stated extraction rule.
- **Interpretation / hypothesis:** author's reasoning, not source fact.
- **Personal reflection:** personal meaning or response.
- **Unverified:** insufficient evidence or unresolved source discrepancy.

For religious / scripture comparisons, distinguish the scripture text, translation, historical context, tradition-specific interpretation, scholarly commentary, and personal reflection. Do not claim that two scriptures or traditions say the same thing when the underlying passages differ.

## Repository ownership

Reuse `packages/corpus`, `packages/research`, `packages/knowledge` and `packages/orm-knowledge` for source snapshots, evidence, claims, review and publication. Extend current research profiles and workflows only where a verifiable gap exists. Do not create a new generic `orm-research` or `orm-puzzle` domain. This issue is a research-method specification, not a second knowledge graph.

## Copyright / attribution safeguards

- Keep quotations short and necessary; prefer source-linked summaries over reproducing full copyrighted pages.
- Preserve source URLs, dates and attribution.
- A reverse-reading / word-pattern result must not reproduce song lyrics or substantial copyrighted text.
- Do not infer a real person's intent from a coincidental letter pattern without independent evidence.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Research record schema separates source, extracted evidence, transformation rule, hypothesis and interpretation.
- [ ] Every pattern claim includes source snapshot / retrieval metadata and a reproducible extraction method.
- [ ] Literal word occurrence is distinguished from words assembled from non-contiguous letters or inferred patterns.
- [ ] Research review supports counter-evidence, alternative explanations and unresolved status.
- [ ] Cross-scripture / cross-source comparisons preserve context and translation provenance.
- [ ] Existing Knowledge / Research owners remain canonical; no duplicate database or addon is introduced.

## References

- [Issue #15 architecture boundary](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/15)
- [Corpus package](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/tree/dev/packages/corpus)
- [Research package](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/tree/dev/packages/research)
- [Knowledge package](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/tree/dev/packages/knowledge)
- [Knowledge addon](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/tree/dev/packages/orm-knowledge)

# Local AI research brief — reproducible evidence and pattern-analysis protocol

## 1. Research stance

The phrase **“find light in the darkness”** is the project's personal motivation for exploration. A meaningful pattern can be a useful question or reflection, but it is not automatically evidence of intentional encoding, prophecy, causation, authorship, coordination or supernatural origin.

The agent's job is to make the observation reproducible and falsifiable, not to persuade the reader that a preferred interpretation must be true.

## 2. Evidence object / source snapshot

For each source record:
- Canonical URL and publisher/author.
- Exact title, edition/version and retrieval timestamp.
- Archived or locally preserved snapshot identifier where legally permitted.
- Source hash, byte length and content type if captured.
- Locator: page, section, heading, paragraph, line or passage.
- Rights/license/allowed-use state.
- Language and script.
- Retrieval method and extraction tool/version.
- Whether the source is live, archived, edited or a synthetic fixture.

Do not treat a URL alone as proof that the page had the same content at an earlier date. If the source changed, retain the exact version/snapshot and compare versions.

## 3. Pattern / puzzle method contract

Every proposed pattern must state:
1. **Question / hypothesis:** what exact observation is being tested?
2. **Input range:** exact source snapshot and text span.
3. **Normalization:** Unicode normalization (e.g. NFC), case handling, diacritics, punctuation, whitespace and line-break rules.
4. **Transformation:** literal search, reverse order, initials/acrostic, final letters, fixed offsets, every-Nth character, parallel columns, word sequence, or another explicit algorithm.
5. **Index convention:** zero-based or one-based; Unicode scalar/code point vs UTF-8 byte offset; preserve original offsets.
6. **Expected output:** what would count as a hit, miss or ambiguous result?
7. **Controls:** compare unrelated passages / shuffled text / other pages; document selection bias.
8. **Alternative explanations:** ordinary language, editing, formatting, coincidence, source truncation, translation choices, or post-hoc selection.
9. **Result:** success, failure, ambiguous or not reproducible.
10. **Interpretation:** a separate hypothesis with limitations and counter-evidence.

Do not quietly change the extraction rule after seeing the result. If the rule changes, create a new method version and rerun the analysis.

## 4. Worked case to re-check — “Written in Reverse”

The project history includes an exploration titled `WRITTEN IN REVERSE — MATTHEW KOMA DISCOGRAPHY`, using the Wikipedia discography page:
`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_Koma_discography`

The conversation explored a possible `MYTH` pattern and phrase/mnemonic wording such as:
`Miracle / You / Tempted / Hysteria`.

A previous page review found that **“MYTH” did not appear as a literal contiguous word** in the inspected page text. Therefore:
- Do not report that Wikipedia literally contains “MYTH” unless a current, exact source snapshot and literal search prove it.
- Treat any assembled letters / separated words as a derived pattern and show the exact character/word positions and extraction rule.
- Re-check the latest page and, where possible, the historical revision that was originally inspected.
- Do not claim the page author intended the pattern without independent evidence.
- Do not reproduce song lyrics or substantial copyrighted discography text; quote only what is necessary and link to the source.

This is an example case for testing the method, not a pre-decided successful discovery.

## 5. Parallel-source / scripture comparison

When comparing texts (including Qur’an, Bible or other religious sources):
- Identify each source's canonical edition, language, translation and textual tradition.
- Align passages by an explicit research question; do not assume similar words mean identical doctrine.
- Distinguish canonical source text, translation, paraphrase, commentary, historical context and personal reflection.
- Record omissions, variant readings, translation choices and disagreement.
- Avoid claims that “all books say the same thing” unless the exact sources and differences support that narrow statement.
- Religious conclusions must not be inferred from a letter puzzle or numeric coincidence.

## 6. Repository reuse

Inspect:
- `packages/corpus` — ingestion, dataset releases, passages and textual witness records.
- `packages/knowledge` — canonical records, source artifacts, provenance, schema versioning and dataset validation/snapshots.
- `packages/research` — assertions, evidence, semantic spans, textual alignment, review, identity reconciliation and candidate analysis.
- `packages/orm-knowledge` — publication, review and research release integration.

Do not create another generic `orm-research`, `orm-puzzle`, source database or shadow evidence graph. Extend current schemas only where a source-backed gap is demonstrated. Respect current privacy, child-protection, immutable-record and rights gates.

## 7. Required output format for an AI research report

- Research question.
- Exact source and version.
- Directly observed facts (with locators).
- Method/transformation version.
- Reproducible steps or small test fixture.
- Output and offsets.
- Controls and alternative explanations.
- Counter-evidence / limitations.
- Interpretation clearly labelled as hypothesis.
- Confidence rationale and reviewer state.
- Publication recommendation: publish, revise, hold or reject.

Acceptance: a second reviewer can reproduce the pattern from the saved snapshot and obtain the same output; literal word hits are not confused with non-contiguous letter assembly; uncertain conclusions remain explicitly uncertain.


## Local AI agent handoff contract

Read this issue and its parent [Issue #15](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/15) in full before acting. Then read the repository rules, especially `.agents/rules/learned-invariants.md`, `docs/tasks/README.md`, `docs/roadmap/ISSUE-SYNC-CONTRACT.md`, and the ADR/package documents linked above. Revalidate the live `dev` SHA and current worktree.

Treat all concepts in this issue as **requirements to investigate**, not evidence of implementation. Label findings as `EXISTS`, `PARTIAL`, `MISSING`, `PROPOSED`, or `UNKNOWN`, each with exact source paths / tests. Search the repository before adding any model, route, package, app, job or UI. Reuse the current canonical owner whenever possible.

Do not edit source, alter TaskOS, install dependencies, change production data, or close issues until the maintainer accepts a concrete implementation slice. When approved, create stable atomic TaskOS records first and follow the issue sync contract. Never mark work done without tests and evidence on the exact dev SHA.

# Historical investigation narrative and worked reproducibility example

## 1. Motivation: “find light in the darkness”

The owner's research exploration uses puzzles, parallel reading and patterns as ways to notice possible relationships that may not be obvious at first glance. The project phrase “find light in the darkness” describes the personal motivation. The research system must preserve curiosity without converting an interesting coincidence into a factual conclusion.

The core engineering question is: **Can another reviewer reproduce exactly what was found, from the same source version, using the same extraction rule?** If not, the result remains unverified.

## 2. Conversation-history trail

Relevant discussions:
- **“Pola Puzzle Wikipedia” — 23 August 2026:** the owner asked for a deep review of a letter/pattern method and wanted the evidence and message summarized before finalizing.
- **“Rancang Ulang Narasi” — 23 August 2026:** the proposed label was “WRITTEN IN REVERSE — MATTHEW KOMA DISCOGRAPHY”, connected to a Wikipedia discography page.
- The discussion included the letter sequence / mnemonic “Miracle / You / Tempted / Hysteria” and the claim that MYTH could be seen near the end or through a parallel pattern.
- During the previous review, the assistant noted that “MYTH” did not appear as a literal contiguous word in the page text inspected at that time. This is a historical observation tied to that particular inspection, not a guarantee about every future revision of the page.

## 3. Worked case: Matthew Koma discography

Source under investigation:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_Koma_discography

A proper research record should contain:
- exact Wikipedia revision ID and retrieval timestamp;
- page title, source URL, revision URL and permitted snapshot/hash;
- extracted text with source locator / section;
- the exact text normalization rules;
- whether the search is a literal contiguous word search or a derived-letter puzzle;
- for any derived pattern: every selected word/letter, exact index/offset, order and extraction rule;
- controls and alternative explanations.

The proposed MYTH interpretation must be represented in separate layers:
- literal source fact: whether the contiguous string “MYTH” occurs in the inspected page;
- derived pattern: whether selected letters or words can be assembled to produce M-Y-T-H under a stated method;
- mnemonic: whether “Miracle / You / Tempted / Hysteria” is a personal wording attached to those letters;
- interpretation: what the researcher thinks the pattern means.

Do not say that the Wikipedia page “contains MYTH” without specifying which of those four meanings is intended. If the pattern relies on selecting non-contiguous words after seeing the desired result, record selection bias and compare it to predeclared controls. Do not infer intent from the page author's work.

## 4. Real-world use case beyond the puzzle

A researcher compares two editions of a source text. The system should show:
1. exact source/version and side-by-side passage alignment;
2. text that was added, removed or translated differently;
3. source facts and quotations with precise locations;
4. a derived pattern only if the transformation can be repeated;
5. uncertainty and alternative interpretations;
6. review decision before publication.

The same process applies to scripture comparison. A Qur'an verse, Bible verse, translation, tafsir, historical commentary and personal reflection are different evidence types. Never merge them into “all texts say exactly the same thing” without an exact, context-preserving analysis.

## 5. Reproducibility requirements

For text-puzzle methods, specify:
- Unicode normalization (NFC/NFKC and reason), case folding, diacritics and punctuation handling.
- Whether bytes, Unicode code points or grapheme clusters are indexed.
- Start/end index convention.
- Source ordering and direction (forward/reverse).
- Selection rule fixed before execution.
- Whether words are contiguous, non-contiguous, acrostic, telestich, parallel-column or every-Nth character.
- Expected outputs and failure conditions.
- Control documents / shuffled text and probability caveats.
- Tool and method version.

A result that changes when punctuation or line breaks change must record that fragility. A result that only appears after repeatedly modifying the rule is a hypothesis, not a discovery.

## 6. Example report language

Good:
“Using revision X, normalized as NFC, we searched the article text for the literal contiguous token MYTH and did not find it. A separate non-contiguous extraction hypothesis selects letters at positions A, B, C and D; the selection rule was defined after exploratory review, so this is a candidate pattern vulnerable to selection bias.”

Not acceptable:
“Wikipedia secretly encoded MYTH and proves the author's intention.”

The agent should be curious, precise and willing to report a negative result.

## 7. Repository implementation boundary

Use Corpus for source/passage capture and versioned datasets; Knowledge for source artifacts/provenance and canonical records; Research for assertions, evidence, semantic spans, alignments and review; ORM-Knowledge for authorized publication/research release. Reuse existing child-protection and privacy gates. Do not build a second scraper, browser archive or shadow knowledge graph unless source review proves a concrete gap.

## Local AI execution instruction

Read the complete issue and parent architecture proposal before producing work. Read the conversation-history narrative, identify which statements are owner intent versus verified source facts, then inspect the current source tree. Do not implement based only on the text in this issue. Mark every discovered capability as EXISTS, PARTIAL, MISSING, PROPOSED or UNKNOWN and cite exact repository paths/tests. Preserve the source wording and uncertainty; never silently “complete” missing requirements by guessing.

Before editing, return a short gap analysis, owner map, files likely to change, dependencies, risks and proposed acceptance evidence. Do not alter source, TaskOS, production data or issue status until the maintainer accepts a concrete implementation slice. After approval, create stable atomic TaskOS records first and follow docs/roadmap/ISSUE-SYNC-CONTRACT.md. Commit only owned paths, use the approved dev workflow, and never report success without verifiable evidence on the exact SHA.

**Parent architecture proposal:** [Issue #15 — Non-overlapping MW-XV expansion](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/15)

**Status:** Product / research specification proposal. This issue captures the project concept and scope; it is not proof that the feature exists or authorization to bypass the repository's TaskOS workflow. After maintainer acceptance, break implementation into atomic records in `docs/tasks/tasks.json` and synchronize them according to `docs/roadmap/ISSUE-SYNC-CONTRACT.md`.

## Goal

Define an artwork-first creation and ingestion workflow that lets the team generate, review, optimize and publish visual assets without forcing every concept through Blender, Three.js, WebGL, or a 3D scene pipeline.

The default deliverable is a high-quality, reviewable 2D artwork asset (PNG / WebP / SVG where appropriate). 3D is optional and requires a concrete product need; it is not the default definition of a successful visual.

## Expected workflow

1. **Brief:** subject, use case, composition, aspect ratio, target viewport, art direction, text-safe areas and prohibited elements.
2. **Generate:** create artwork variants using the approved image-generation workflow; keep prompt / source provenance and output metadata.
3. **Review:** human selection, visual quality, readability, original-design / rights review, safety and brand consistency.
4. **Prepare:** optimize sizes and formats; create transparent or layered variants only when useful; preserve source master.
5. **Register:** add approved files to the one canonical `packages/assets/manifest.json` and existing provenance / license metadata.
6. **Preview:** use existing UI Catalog, asset browser and scene harness to inspect the artwork in its intended UI context.
7. **Verify:** run existing asset validation, duplicate/orphan, dimensions, file-size and consumer-budget checks before use.

## Product boundary

- Extend `packages/assets` for master assets, variants, provenance, licensing and validation.
- Extend the existing `apps/ui-catalog` Creative Lab for review / preview tooling.
- Reuse `packages/ui` for rendering components and the existing layered 2D / sprite / scene primitives when a composition needs them.
- Do not create a second asset manager, a new asset database, or a separate Creative Studio app.
- Do not create a mandatory 3D scene or runtime package.
- Do not make AI artwork-generation requests implicitly trigger scene-runtime or 3D code generation.

The repository already has the W2 asset pipeline, W4 environment layers, W5 2D scene/runtime foundations, and W7 Creative Lab tasks. This issue must complement those tasks, not reimplement them. In particular, keep existing W7 Asset Browser / Character Studio / Environment Inspector / Timeline / QA work in its canonical task pack.

## Requirements

- One canonical manifest and one provenance / licensing source of truth.
- Distinguish generated source master from derived/resized/optimized outputs.
- Track prompt/version/source metadata without leaking private user content or secrets.
- Original, rights-cleared art only; do not reproduce copyrighted character designs or imitate a living artist's distinctive style.
- Keep text and dynamic UI labels separate from baked artwork lettering unless decorative lettering is intentionally part of the source asset.
- Transparent alpha, responsive crops and layered exports are optional asset capabilities, not mandatory for every image.
- Human approval before an asset is promoted from draft to canonical production use.
- Avoid inaccurate “3D” previews that are only a flat poster placed in a 3D viewer.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Artwork-only flow can produce and register PNG / WebP / SVG as appropriate without 3D tooling.
- [ ] Asset variants trace to one canonical source master.
- [ ] Provenance, rights/license and review state are validated.
- [ ] UI Catalog preview is reused and the current Creative Lab task pack is not duplicated.
- [ ] Existing asset validation / performance budgets remain enforced.
- [ ] No separate asset manager, app or scene runtime is created without a demonstrated need.

- [Creative Lab spec](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/blob/dev/MWXV_ULTRA_COMPLETE_VISUAL_UNIVERSE_AUTONOMOUS_PACK/CREATIVE_LAB.md)

# Local AI production brief — artwork-first visual asset pipeline

## 1. Default output and decision rule

The normal creative deliverable is a **static 2D artwork**. Use PNG for transparent/high-fidelity masters where appropriate, WebP/AVIF for optimized raster delivery where supported by existing asset rules, and SVG for suitable original vector artwork. Do not force an artwork request into Blender, Three.js, WebGL, Pixi, Rive, Live2D, a 3D model, or a new renderer.

The existing repository already has the canonical asset package, manifest/provenance rules, 2D layered environment exports, sprite player, LayeredScene and UI Catalog scene harness. The purpose here is to make AI-generated artwork easy to admit safely into that system—not to rebuild that infrastructure.

## 2. Required artwork brief (before generation)

Every asset request should have a short structured brief:
- Stable proposed asset ID / descriptive slug.
- Subject and intended product use.
- Audience / context and prohibited content.
- Aspect ratio and pixel target (poster, banner, card, avatar, background, icon).
- Composition, focal point and text-safe zone.
- Art direction, palette, line weight, rendering style and atmosphere.
- Whether transparent alpha is required.
- Whether the image needs layers/variants or is intentionally one flattened artwork.
- Dynamic UI copy that must stay outside the art.
- Copyright / reference constraints.
- Output variants and approval owner.

Do not make missing details up as product facts. Use reasonable visual defaults only for non-semantic choices and mark them as proposed.

## 3. Generation-to-production workflow

1. **Brief:** agree intended asset role, output dimensions/ratio and exclusions.
2. **Generate:** request one or more visual candidates using the approved generation tool. Preserve prompt/version/model provenance allowed by the tool and project policy.
3. **Inspect:** visually check anatomy/proportions, artifacts, text, Arabic glyph accuracy, composition, crop safety, contrast and brand coherence.
4. **Select:** a human chooses the candidate; the agent must not silently mark generated output as approved.
5. **Prepare:** preserve the best source master, create optimized derivatives, optional transparent/layered variants and responsive crops.
6. **Register:** add the canonical asset ID and all variants to the existing `packages/assets/manifest.json` / provenance source. Never create a parallel JSON asset catalog.
7. **Preview:** use UI Catalog and the actual intended consumer. Compare desktop/mobile, light/dark and reduced-motion if relevant.
8. **Validate:** run the current asset validation, duplicate ID/path, orphan, dimensions, provenance/license, size and bundle-budget gates.
9. **Promote:** only a reviewed, licensed asset enters canonical production use.

## 4. Asset lineage and metadata

One source master may have multiple derived variants. Every derivative must link back to its source master and record:
- Asset ID, path, kind, format, dimensions, bytes, aspect ratio and alpha state.
- Variant role (source, optimized, thumbnail, responsive crop, transparent layer, sprite frame).
- Source hash and derivative hash.
- Prompt provenance where allowed; generator/tool version; generation date.
- Human reviewer and review state.
- Rights/license/attribution status.
- Consumer references and bundle/performance budget.
- Focal point, crop-safe and text-safe metadata where useful.

Do not store provider secrets, private prompts, private attachments or sensitive user data in public manifests. A passing structural validator does not prove legal rights; keep explicit review.

## 5. Artwork vs scene / 3D boundaries

- A poster is a poster; do not fake a 3D scene by rotating a flat plane.
- Static artwork can be consumed directly by Board/UI without scene runtime.
- Use the existing 2D LayeredScene/sprite system only when layering, parallax, responsive depth or animation genuinely adds value.
- Layers are optional and should be split only when independent motion/editing is required.
- Use SVG only for shapes that suit vector output; do not force complex raster painting into SVG.
- Sound is opt-in, licensed and separately sourced; no music is implied by an artwork request.
- Do not add dependencies or SDKs before proving a use case, license compatibility and bundle impact.

## 6. Existing task pack reconciliation

Read `CREATIVE_LAB.md` and `MWXV_ULTRA_COMPLETE_VISUAL_UNIVERSE_AUTONOMOUS_PACK/TASKS.md` before implementation. Continue the open Creative Lab work already present there (including W6-003/W6-004/W6-006/W6-007 and W7-003–W7-007 as recorded on the reviewed branch). Do not clone those into a second backlog or mark them complete from this issue.

The user preference is explicit: do not force 3DJS or similar frameworks where a generated artwork image is sufficient. The preferred outcome is good artwork plus correct ingestion and visual QA, not an unnecessarily complicated runtime.

## 7. Acceptance / QA cases

- A developer can generate, inspect and register a static artwork without opening 3D software.
- Source and derivatives are linked, repeatable and hash-verifiable.
- No artwork is promoted without a human review state and rights/provenance metadata.
- Arabic/sacred text is checked independently; generated glyph errors are never treated as authoritative text.
- UI text, metrics and interactive controls remain accessible live UI, not baked pixels.
- Mobile crops do not cut important subjects or safe text areas.
- Asset validation and bundle budgets pass for the actual consuming app.


## Local AI agent handoff contract

Read this issue and its parent [Issue #15](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/15) in full before acting. Then read the repository rules, especially `.agents/rules/learned-invariants.md`, `docs/tasks/README.md`, `docs/roadmap/ISSUE-SYNC-CONTRACT.md`, and the ADR/package documents linked above. Revalidate the live `dev` SHA and current worktree.

# Narrative, conversation history and real production examples

## 1. Why the owner requested this pipeline

The owner has repeatedly encountered a mismatch between the desired visual output and an overly complicated implementation approach. The need is often to create one strong poster, banner, scene background or artwork asset—not to build a 3D engine.

The key conversation is **“Create UI Mockup” — 15 November 2026**. The owner asked for alternatives to Blender that AI could use, then challenged whether the mockup could simply use generated PNG artwork. The explicit direction was to give the AI a prompt that says **use the ARTWORK itself and do not force Three.js / 3DJS or similar frameworks when the result is poor**.

This issue turns that preference into a repeatable production rule.

## 2. Real-world examples

### Example A — campaign / film-style poster
A designer asks for a vertical 9:16 GOD PROMISE or MoonWitness poster. The right output may simply be:
- one high-resolution artwork master,
- a mobile optimized WebP,
- a text-safe area,
- a separate live-text title and source block in the UI.

There is no need for a 3D model, camera system, lighting rig or interactive runtime if the poster is static.

### Example B — Moon City background
A homepage needs a moonlit city skyline. If it only needs a static hero image, register one approved artwork. If foreground, skyline and moon need independent parallax or responsive reordering, use the existing layered asset/scene foundation. Do not create layers just to make the asset sound more advanced.

### Example C — character reference sheet
A character needs a stable appearance for future illustrations. Generate an original reference sheet, then preserve one canonical master and separately approved pose / expression / clothing variants. Do not force a skeletal rig or Live2D model unless animation is actually required by a consumer.

### Example D — icon / UI illustration
A tiny icon may be better as a hand-authored SVG or existing icon component, not as a giant AI raster image. Choose the format based on the asset's actual role.

## 3. Prompting contract for a local AI

The agent should understand the difference between:
- **Generate artwork:** use an image generator and produce a rendered visual file.
- **Build an interactive component:** implement React/UI with real controls and accessible states.
- **Build an animated scene:** use the existing 2D scene and sprite pipeline only when animation materially improves the experience.
- **Build 3D:** only when real geometry, camera, lighting or spatial interaction is explicitly required.

A useful default instruction for the artwork-only case:

“Create or select a high-quality original 2D artwork asset that satisfies the visual brief. Deliver a static PNG/WebP/SVG as appropriate, with the intended composition and responsive safe area. Do not create a Three.js, WebGL, Blender, 3D model, camera or scene runtime. Keep dynamic text and buttons as UI elements outside the artwork. Register the approved master and derivatives in the existing canonical Assets manifest with provenance and license review.”

The agent must still decide whether the requested deliverable is actually an image, UI component or editable structured asset. A rendered PNG cannot replace a working button, text editor, database record or interactive timeline.

## 4. Current repository reuse

Before adding code, inspect:
- packages/assets canonical manifest, schema, validators, provenance and license records.
- the existing asset duplicate / orphan / dimension / bundle-budget gates.
- W2 asset pipeline and W4 layer exports.
- W5 typed 2D scene, LayeredScene, SpritePlayer and playback/camera/timeline primitives.
- UI Catalog Creative Lab specification and pending W6/W7 tasks.

An earlier task pack explicitly chose the current 2D scene approach and skipped a third-party rig engine POC because it did not justify the cost. That decision should be respected until a new, concrete use case changes it.

## 5. Quality examples and failure cases

Reject or send back for review:
- low-resolution output stretched to full-screen hero size;
- cropped character faces / typography at mobile breakpoints;
- invented or malformed Arabic calligraphy presented as verified text;
- copyrighted anime characters copied from screenshots;
- an image with baked-in dynamic buttons, fake metrics or unreadable source notes;
- a flat poster rotated in a 3D viewport and described as a 3D environment;

- **GOD PROMISE:** a structured Qur’an-grounded reflection / poster / short-form content format.
- **ROCKSOUL:** a personal reflection, self-maintenance, learning and creative narrative framework.

Both must remain source-attributed editorial projects. A personal reflection, visual metaphor, mnemonic, or creative taxonomy must never be presented as Qur’anic text, hadith, tafsir, or established scientific fact unless independently verified and attributed.

Preferred content structure:

3. Relevant Asmaul Husna pair according to the project's **editorial mnemonic**: Surah number → first name; ayah number → second name. This mapping is a creative format convention, not a religiously established exegesis rule; flag it as such and review before publication.
4. Brief explanation / reflection with clear separation between the verse, translation, source context, and the author's personal reflection.

- `IF I DIE - I'LL BE BACK` / QS Al-Hujurat 49:15–17 concept: treat the slogan as metaphorical editorial copy, not a promise about literal return or a factual claim.
- Personal statements / vows must be explicitly labelled as the author's own words, not a divine message.

The Duha sun-angle idea (including the remembered ~45° visual) is a visual/educational prompt only. Do not turn it into a universal fiqh ruling or exact prayer-time instruction. Prayer-time and legal guidance need a reliable local scholarly source and proper context.

## 4. ROCKSOUL — concept layers

Preserve the creative project names:
- `GOD-PROMISE — Rock SOUL`
- `Maintenance 4 Pilar of soul / Djiwa Alami`
- `AR-RUH Absurd Teori`
- `ANGEL WITH SHOTGUN`
- `HISTA`

Treat “Merawat sebuah Kaca” and “self reflection first” as metaphors for self-review and accountability. The remembered `nafs – fisikal – infrastructure` and “input = output / must same path” are conceptual diagrams, not validated anatomy, psychology, neurology or a literal map of the soul.

The remembered four-pillar maintenance framework needs an explicit definition for each pillar before implementation; do not invent missing pillar names. HISTA means:
- Hikmah
- Isti’anah
- Sains
- Tawakal
- Amanah

The motivation formula `faith × prayer × knowledge × effort × patience` is a memorable slogan, not a scientific equation or measurable human-performance formula.

### Medical / scientific boundary
The previous breathing-path narrative (nose → filtering → brain orchestration → multiple brain/heart/lung pathways) is not an approved physiology model. Do not reproduce it as established science. If the subject is breathing, illness, Histatin, lysozyme or anatomy, cite reliable medical/scientific sources, separate hypotheses from established mechanisms, and do not prescribe this framework as treatment. Healthcare diagnosis/treatment remains with qualified professionals; spiritual practices may be described as personal support, not a substitute.

## 5. ANGEL WITH SHOTGUN / symbolic narrative system

Preserve these as creative episode / analysis labels where useful:
- `BULLSHIT TACTIC — LIP SERVICES`
- `KILL DAJJAL` (a narrative title; must not become a real-world violent instruction or call to attack anyone).
- Hero / Isa / Jesus / Christus / Messianic narratives.
- Four remembered Dajjal framework colors: red = visible / Ẓāhir, green = hidden / Bāṭin, blue = false religious-looking / “Hikmah” illusion, white = Revelation / Yajuj-Majuj / dead-end. This is the author's project taxonomy only, not a canonical Islamic creed or scholarly classification.
- The remembered HERO 47 framework (L4 Inner Human, L5 God-Conscious, L6 Ihsan Human, L7 Rasul / Al-Ma‘rifah) must be clearly presented as personal role/metaphor language, never as a claim to prophethood or equivalence to Rasulullah SAW.

Any episode about justice, Dajjal, prophets or sacred history must avoid incitement, dehumanization and claims of personal authority. Prefer evidence, ethical reflection and non-graphic symbolic art. Do not depict Allah or visually portray prophets as identifiable characters.

## 6. Content workflow

Draft → source verification → theological/context review → scientific/legal/copyright review where relevant → visual review → human approval → publication. Record every revision and reviewer decision. An AI local agent may:
- propose a template-compliant draft,
- flag missing sources or unsupported statements,
- create citation and claim checklists,
- suggest a visual brief and alt text,
- compare versions.

An AI agent may not invent Quranic verses, hadith, translations, scholarly consensus, scientific explanations, personal testimony or approval status.

## 7. Acceptance tests

- A reader can identify exactly which words are Qur’an, translation, tafsir, author reflection, metaphor or AI suggestion.
- A cited verse resolves to the exact source/edition and correct ayah.
- The Asma mnemonic is visibly labelled as a project convention.
- Du’a meets the project's length/opening rule without fabricating a sourced prayer.
- Scientific/medical claims have source and reviewer state or are labelled unverified.
- Visual prompt avoids sacred depiction and uses rights-cleared original artwork.
- Draft, review, rejected, approved and published states are auditable and use the existing Knowledge publication pipeline.


## Local AI agent handoff contract

Read this issue and its parent [Issue #15](https://github.com/A-L-L-A-H/mw-xv/issues/15) in full before acting. Then read the repository rules, especially `.agents/rules/learned-invariants.md`, `docs/tasks/README.md`, `docs/roadmap/ISSUE-SYNC-CONTRACT.md`, and the ADR/package documents linked above. Revalidate the live `dev` SHA and current worktree.

Treat all concepts in this issue as **requirements to investigate**, not evidence of implementation. Label findings as `EXISTS`, `PARTIAL`, `MISSING`, `PROPOSED`, or `UNKNOWN`, each with exact source paths / tests. Search the repository before adding any model, route, package, app, job or UI. Reuse the current canonical owner whenever possible.

Do not edit source, alter TaskOS, install dependencies, change production data, or close issues until the maintainer accepts a concrete implementation slice. When approved, create stable atomic TaskOS records first and follow the issue sync contract. Never mark work done without tests and evidence on the exact dev SHA.

# Editorial narrative, conversation history and worked content examples

## 1. Why two editorial tracks are needed

The owner's discussions produced two related but distinct content families:
- **GOD PROMISE** is a structured scripture-referenced poster / reflection format.
- **ROCKSOUL** is a personal reflection and creative framework about self-maintenance, learning, responsibility and narrative analysis.

Both may use the same Content Studio, visual pipeline and Knowledge publication workflow. They must not be collapsed into one theological or scientific claim system. A GOD PROMISE poster can quote or reference a religious source; a ROCKSOUL diagram may be a personal metaphor. Those are different kinds of statements and need different review.

## 2. Conversation-history references

The relevant discussions include:
- **GOD PROMISE poster / film concepts — 16–19 August 2026:** user developed poster copy around religious stories and personal statements; requested clear caveats distinguishing the author's statement from claims about scripture.
- **“Merapikan Konsep Rock Soul” — 16 September 2026:** user supplied “Maintenance 4 Pilar of soul Djiwa Alami”, “Merawat sebuah Kaca”, “self reflection first”, “nafs-fisikal-infrastructure”, input/output and breathing-path notes, then asked for cross-check and finalization.
- The project history also includes GOD PROMISE themes such as “Find Me In Everything”, “Friend with ALLAH”, “Al-Halim”, “Best Duha Time”, HISTA, Histatin & Lysozyme, and “R.E. NOT LIE / REAL EVIDENCE — NOT A LIE”.

These history references are context, not evidence that the underlying religious, scientific or medical assertions have been verified.

## 3. Concrete GOD PROMISE example: an editorial record

A draft about a verse should look like this:

**Header:** GOD PROMISE — [short English title]

**Source block:** exact surah/ayah locator, Arabic source edition, translation text, translator, URL or corpus release, and review state.

**Context block:** brief context from a named tafsir or other verified source. If no reliable context source is available, explicitly say “context not yet reviewed”.

**Asmaul Husna block:** selected names, original Arabic, transliteration and meaning, with sources. The project may use its remembered convention of Surah number → first name and ayah number → second name, but this must be labelled as a project mnemonic, not a divinely established numeric key.

**Reflection block:** author's own response, clearly labelled “personal reflection”.

**Visual block:** title/typography/mood/artwork brief, without depicting Allah or turning an analogy into a theological claim.

**Du'a block:** no more than one or two sentences, beginning with “biiznillah” and including the selected Asmaul Husna, as the user's preferred editorial format. Do not fabricate a canonical hadith or claim the wording is a transmitted prayer unless sourced.

### Historical draft references for regression / content recovery

The conversation memory recalls prior draft topics:
- QS 4:75, paired in a previous GOD PROMISE draft with Al-Quddus + Aẓ-Ẓāhir.
- QS 18:19 / 18:47, previously paired with Al-Fattah + Al-Wadud.
- Other referenced passages/topics include QS 12:59, 13:13 / 13:22 / 13:28 / 13:34, 9:59, 11:97 / 11:111 / 11:123 and 3:127.
- The Isa / Jesus narrative includes the user's recurring point that miracles are gifts granted by Allah, not proof that Isa is God; this must be framed as the user's Islamic editorial position and checked against the exact Qur'anic passages and the relevant Bible text / interpretation when comparative claims are made.

These are **draft recovery pointers only**. Re-open the exact prior source material, verify verse references, check the actual numbered Asma list, and do not assume that a remembered pairing or interpretation is automatically correct.

## 4. Project-specific naming and visual style

Preserve these labels:
- GOD PROMISE
- GOD PROMISE / SF (Share Feeling)
- GOD PROMISE — Qāf Kāf kahf Kun
- Arabic motif: قاف • كاف • الكهف • كُنْ
- “Find Me In Everything”
- “Friend with ALLAH”
- “R.E. NOT LIE / REAL EVIDENCE — NOT A LIE”

Use English final poster copy when the brief requests English, while source metadata and Indonesian explanation can remain available to editors. Avoid placeholder titles and repeated paragraphs. Keep the poster readable; a visually dense source/reference section may belong in a companion note rather than on the artwork.

## 5. ROCKSOUL worked example: mirror maintenance

A safe conceptual article can use “Merawat sebuah Kaca” as the central metaphor:
- The mirror represents self-reflection, not a medical or spiritual instrument.
- “Self reflection first” means examine one's own assumptions and behavior before judging others.
- “nafs – fisikal – infrastructure” can be shown as three conceptual layers if the author defines each term. The diagram must be titled as an author's framework, not a proven anatomy of the soul.
- “Input = output / must same path” can be explained as a personal consistency principle, not a physical law.
- The four pillars need owner confirmation. Do not invent the missing names or silently substitute a different four-pillar model.
- HISTA is the five-part mnemonic Hikmah, Isti’anah, Sains, Tawakal, Amanah. It is not four pillars and should not be conflated with the four-pillar framework.
- “faith × prayer × knowledge × effort × patience” is a motivational formula, not a scientific equation.

## 6. ROCKSOUL scientific and medical review example

The previous breathing-path description referred to nose filtering, brain orchestration, cerebellum, qalb, right/left brain, throat, heart/lungs and response pathways. That is not a validated physiological map. A local AI must not turn that description into an educational medical infographic without rewriting it against reliable anatomy/physiology sources and obtaining review.

The same rule applies to Histatin and Lysozyme: explain only what a reliable scientific source supports; record species/tissue/context and distinguish a study result from a general clinical conclusion. Do not suggest changing medication or treatment. The user's own corrected note was that illness treatment should follow a doctor's prescription first; the platform should preserve this safety correction.

## 7. ANGEL WITH SHOTGUN / narrative examples

Project labels remembered from the history include:
- “ANGEL WITH SHOTGUN — BULLSHIT TACTIC / LIP SERVICES”.
- “KILL DAJJAL” as an episode/story title.
- A hero narrative referencing Isa / Jesus / Christus / Messianic tradition.
- A four-colour Dajjal concept taxonomy (red Ẓāhir, green Bāṭin, blue false religious-looking “Hikmah” illusion, white Revelation / Yajuj Majuj / total dead end).
- “HERO 47”: L4 Inner Human, L5 God-Conscious, L6 Ihsan Human, L7 Rasul / Al-Ma‘rifah.

These are editorial / symbolic taxonomies from the owner's project, not a canonical creed, scholarly classification, or authority claim. A local agent must label them as project concepts, seek source review for religious assertions, and avoid incitement, real-world threats, graphic imagery or depicting sacred figures as identifiable characters.

## 8. Content lifecycle and roles

Use:
- Draft owner: author/editor.
- Source verifier: checks exact text, edition and locator.
- Context reviewer: verifies tafsir / historical / comparative claims.
- Science reviewer: checks medical/scientific statements.
- Visual reviewer: checks artwork, typography, accessibility and copyright.
- Publisher: authorized human who approves publication.

An LLM may propose, classify, compare, summarize or flag gaps. It cannot mark its own source verification or human review as passed. All statuses must be explicit and auditable.

## Local AI execution instruction

Read the complete issue and parent architecture proposal before producing work. Read the conversation-history narrative, identify which statements are owner intent versus verified source facts, then inspect the current source tree. Do not implement based only on the text in this issue. Mark every discovered capability as EXISTS, PARTIAL, MISSING, PROPOSED or UNKNOWN and cite exact repository paths/tests. Preserve the source wording and uncertainty; never silently “complete” missing requirements by guessing.

Before editing, return a short gap analysis, owner map, files likely to change, dependencies, risks and proposed acceptance evidence. Do not alter source, TaskOS, production data or issue status until the maintainer accepts a concrete implementation slice. After approval, create stable atomic TaskOS records first and follow docs/roadmap/ISSUE-SYNC-CONTRACT.md. Commit only owned paths, use the approved dev workflow, and never report success without verifiable evidence on the exact SHA.

**Status:** Product / research specification proposal. This issue captures the project concept and scope; it is not proof that the feature exists or authorization to bypass the repository's TaskOS workflow. After maintainer acceptance, break implementation into atomic records in `docs/tasks/tasks.json` and synchronize them according to `docs/roadmap/ISSUE-SYNC-CONTRACT.md`.

## Product identity

- Product name: **MoonWitness**
- Indonesian meaning: **BULAN BERSAKSI**
- Original working tagline (preserve as source wording): **“When The moon high/rises,we Share Message.”**
- Suggested editorial refinement for review, not a replacement until approved: “When the Moon rises, we share messages.”
- Related framing used in the concept: **RADIO — MoonWitness** and **MyLuft Says**.

MoonWitness is a message-sharing and community experience concept. The moon / moon phase is a visual and editorial motif for moments of reflection and sharing, not an astrology, prediction, or supernatural-claim engine.

## Product experience to specify

1. **Message sharing:** create, curate, and share short messages / signals with explicit audience and visibility controls.
2. **Radio:** a MoonWitness audio/radio experience, with a separate product decision on whether the first release is on-demand audio, scheduled programmes, or live streaming.
3. **Community:** membership, follows, reactions and discussions, using the ownership boundary in Issue #15.
4. **Experience / progression:** game-like levels, stages, missions and achievements, with real-world reward claims only after eligibility, fulfilment, safety and abuse controls are defined.
5. **Visual identity:** expressive typography, playful/funky line effects, atmospheric moon visuals, and a respectful presentation that does not require character faces.
6. **Audience:** accessible and playful for younger audiences while providing age-appropriate privacy, moderation, reporting, guardian / child-safety requirements where applicable, and safe defaults.

## Data ownership — no duplicate systems

- Published editorial content and revisions: existing `orm-knowledge` / corpus / publication.
- Social relationships and interactions: proposed `orm-community` in Issue #15.
- XP, levels, achievements and reward claims: proposed `orm-experience` in Issue #15.
- User identity: existing base/auth.
- Notifications: existing `orm-notification`.
- Audio/artwork files and provenance: existing `orm-storage` and `packages/assets`.
- Radio scheduling / streaming data must not be assigned a new ORM package until the product requirements show that existing publication, jobs, storage and integration contracts are insufficient.

## Decisions and deliverables

- Define the key user journeys: discover → compose → preview → share → receive feedback → revisit.
- Define message types, visibility, retention, sharing controls and moderation lifecycle.
- Define Radio MVP (on-demand vs scheduled vs live) and rights / provenance requirements for audio.
- Define levels, mission triggers and reward fulfilment without duplicating project tasks or inventing engagement metrics.
- Define safety and privacy requirements before launching public or youth-facing surfaces.
- Produce a content model / screen map that points to the canonical owners above; do not invent new stores for existing data.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Approved product statement and tagline decision recorded.
- [ ] Message, Radio, Community and Experience journeys are separately scoped.
- [ ] Public/private visibility, reporting, moderation and age-appropriate safety decisions are documented.
- [ ] Radio MVP and audio rights/provenance requirements are explicit.
- [ ] Every persistent entity has one canonical owner; no Community / Publication / Notification / WhatsApp duplication.
- [ ] Only accepted implementation tasks are added to TaskOS.

# Local AI product brief — MoonWitness

## 1. Product purpose and interpretation

MoonWitness (Indonesian concept gloss: **BULAN BERSAKSI**) is a message-sharing and shared-experience platform concept. The moon is a visual metaphor for a time/space in which people reflect and share messages. The platform is not an astrology engine, a prediction service, or a claim that the moon itself speaks or validates messages.

Preserve the original working tagline exactly in source notes:
`When The moon high/rises,we Share Message.`
A proposed copy edit is “When the Moon rises, we share messages.” The AI must not silently replace the original; record a human decision on the final wording.

Keep these concept labels as metadata / editorial identity:
- `RADIO — MoonWitness`
- `MyLuft Says`
- `MoonWitness = BULAN BERSAKSI`
- “When the Moon rises, we share messages” (candidate polished English line)

## 2. Core journey and product surfaces

Design the product around a clear loop:
1. **Discover:** browse approved public messages, channels, radio programmes and community spaces.
2. **Compose:** create a short message / signal with title, body, language, audience, visibility, optional artwork/audio and source attribution.
3. **Preview:** inspect how the message appears on desktop and mobile before publication.
4. **Share:** publish to a selected audience with explicit visibility, reuse and retention settings.
5. **Interact:** receive a reaction, reply or notification; apply report/block/mute rules.
6. **Return:** revisit saved items, follow a channel or continue a mission/experience stage.

Treat "message" carefully. An editorial message/post should reuse an existing Knowledge publication/story where possible. A private chat is a separate requirement and must not be silently inferred from the slogan; WhatsApp is currently an external integration and cannot be repurposed into a generic first-party DM system without a separate decision.

Recommended surface map (validate against current routes before coding):
- Public Home / Discover.
- Message / Publication detail.
- Channel / Community detail.
- Compose / Preview / Submit.
- Radio landing and programme/episode page.
- User profile and preferences.
- Mission / achievements / reward-claim pages.
- Moderation/report workflow.
- Admin Board views for content review, community safety and reward operations.

## 3. Radio scope decision — required before schema

The word “Radio” is not enough to justify a package. Compare three product modes:

| Mode | Minimum concepts | Operational consequence |
|---|---|---|
| On-demand audio | Audio publication, transcript/caption, artwork, duration, rights, player | May fit existing publication + asset/storage |
| Scheduled programme | Programme/series, episode, schedule/timezone, host/editor, replay | May need schedule metadata and jobs; verify existing contracts |
| Live streaming | Stream session, stream endpoint/provider, live state, moderation, recording/replay, reliability | Requires streaming infrastructure and a separate threat/operations design |

For each mode record user value, technical complexity, rights/licensing, content moderation, reliability, storage/egress costs and accessibility. Do not decide that UI audio components equal a broadcast backend. Defer `orm-broadcast` until a concrete gap and model boundary are approved.

## 4. Gamified user experience

Preserve the concept of stages, levels, experience and real-world rewards, but distinguish:
- Product engagement (a user completing a meaningful activity).
- XP/achievement (an auditable progression record owned by `orm-experience`).
- Project work (owned by `orm-project`).
- Editorial/community activity (owned by Knowledge / Community).
- Reward approval and fulfilment (separate operational workflow).

Avoid manipulative streaks, infinite engagement loops, public popularity rankings, or rewards tied to sensitive personal disclosures. Never award progress based on unverified client claims. Define anti-abuse and accessibility alternatives for every mission.

## 5. Audience, safeguarding and privacy

The early concept uses playful, game-like language and references a young audience. Any public surface must be age-appropriate by design:
- Data minimization; collect no unnecessary exact location, school, contact details or sensitive profile data.
- Default private/minimum-visibility settings for younger users; public posting must be controlled by the product's age/consent policy.
- Blocking, reporting, moderation, rate limits, abuse response and safe contact boundaries.
- No location reveal, unsafe reward fulfilment, direct contact prompts or incentives that ask minors to meet strangers.
- No public leaderboard that exposes identity or encourages harmful comparison.
- Determine whether parental/guardian consent or restricted child accounts are required with legal/product review before launch.
- Use the existing child-protection gate and privacy/revocation controls where relevant; verify their current contracts before integration.

## 6. Visual and editorial direction

The concept prefers a playful/funky line treatment, expressive typography, atmospheric moon/phase imagery and a respectful presentation that does not depend on depicting faces. A playful look must not make the app harder to read or bypass accessibility. Use original, rights-cleared artwork from the canonical Assets package. Keep dynamic copy and labels as UI text; do not bake data or false engagement metrics into art.

Do not invent users, countries, audience reach, active listeners, ratings, or community statistics. Empty, loading, error and zero states must be honest.

## 7. AI agent design tasks

The local agent should deliver, in order:
1. A one-page product statement and glossary (message, publication, community, radio, mission, experience, reward).
2. Journey map and route/screen inventory with current-vs-proposed labels.
3. Radio MVP decision record (on-demand / scheduled / live / defer).
4. Content/data ownership table; every persistent field must have one owner.
5. Visibility, retention, safety, moderation and privacy matrix.
6. A feature slice proposal with dependencies and acceptance tests.
7. TaskOS decomposition only after maintainer approval.

Suggested discovery commands: inspect `apps/board/src/app`, `apps/api/src/addons/registry.ts`, `packages/orm-knowledge`, `packages/orm-notification`, `packages/orm-whatsapp`, `packages/assets`, existing child-protection routes and `packages/orm-project`. Do not assume the route names from this issue already exist.

## 8. Acceptance scenarios

- A user can distinguish a published message from a private message.
- A publication's revisions/source evidence are still stored once in Knowledge.
- A reaction creates one canonical interaction and cannot be duplicated by retry.
- A blocked/reporting user cannot continue unwanted interaction.
- A reward is not issued from a client-forged XP value.
- Audio has transcript/caption and clear rights state before public publication.
- Public/user analytics are derived from real events and are not seeded as fabricated production data.
